title.zh: 卷244 列傳三十一 赵开心 杨义 林起龙 朱克简 王命岳 李森先 李裀 季开生 张煊
title.en: Volume 244 Biographies 31: Zhao Kaixin, Yang Yi, Lin Qilong, Zhu Kejian, Wang Mingyue, Li Senxian, Li Yin, Ji Kaisheng, Zhang Xuan
title.raw: 卷244 列傳三十一 赵开心 杨义 林起龙 朱克简 王命岳 李森先 李裀 季开生 张煊

sentences.zh: =趙開心=趙開心，字靈伯，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: =Zhao Kaixin= Zhao Kaixin, style Lingbo, native of Changsha, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kaixin, whose style was Lingbo, came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，官至兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the Ming Chongzhen reign, he reached the post of vice director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree under the Ming in the Chongzhen reign and rose to vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，授陝西道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, he was appointed censor of the Shaanxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1644 he was appointed censor of the Shaanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 是歲有自稱故明皇太子者，令故明貴妃袁氏及故東宮官屬內監等視之，皆言不相識。

translations.literal: That year there was one who claimed to be the former Ming crown prince; he was made to be viewed by the former Ming consort Yuan and former Eastern Palace officials and eunuchs, all of whom said they did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: That year a man claiming to be the former Ming crown prince was brought before Consort Yuan of the deposed dynasty and former Eastern Palace officials and eunuchs, none of whom recognized him.

sentences.zh: 開心及給事中硃徽疏請詳審，下法司，自承為京師民楊玉。

translations.literal: Kaixin and supervising secretary Zhu Hui memorialized requesting detailed investigation; the case was sent to the judiciary, and the man confessed that he was Yang Yu, a commoner of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kaixin and supervising secretary Zhu Hui petitioned for a thorough investigation; when the case reached the judiciary, the man admitted he was Yang Yu, a Beijing commoner.

sentences.zh: 以開心疏言「太子若存，明朝之幸」，論死，上命免之。

translations.literal: Because Kaixin's memorial said "If the crown prince still lives, it would be the fortune of the Ming dynasty," he was sentenced to death, but the emperor ordered him pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Kaixin was sentenced to death for writing in his memorial that "if the crown prince survives, it would be the Ming dynasty's salvation," but the emperor spared him.

sentences.zh: 二年，疏言：「刑部治庶獄，數日即結正。

translations.literal: In the second year, he memorialized: "The Ministry of Punishments handles ordinary cases and concludes them within a few days.
translations.idiomatic: In 1645 he submitted a memorial: "The Ministry of Punishments resolves ordinary cases within days,

sentences.zh: 惟自別衙門發送者，恆不時讞決，久置獄中。

translations.literal: Only those sent from other yamens are constantly not adjudicated in timely fashion and left long in prison.
translations.idiomatic: yet cases referred from other offices are routinely left undecided and prisoners held indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 請令所司五日一稽核，當鞫當釋，勿使留滯。

translations.literal: I request that the responsible offices be ordered to audit once every five days, to try or release as appropriate, and not allow detention to linger.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that responsible offices audit cases every five days, try or release prisoners as appropriate, and prevent indefinite detention.

sentences.zh: 並請通飭諸行省撫按遵行。

translations.literal: I also request that governors-general and censors in all provinces be generally instructed to comply.
translations.idiomatic: I also ask that governors and provincial censors throughout the empire be ordered to follow suit.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡視南城。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to inspect the southern city.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to inspect the southern wards of the capital.

sentences.zh: 滿洲兵初入關，畏痘，有染輒死。

translations.literal: When Manchu troops first entered the pass, they feared smallpox; those infected died at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Manchu troops first entered China, they feared smallpox and usually died upon infection.

sentences.zh: 京師民有痘者，令移居出城，杜傳染。

translations.literal: Commoners in the capital who had smallpox were ordered to move outside the city to block transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing residents with smallpox were ordered to relocate outside the city walls to prevent spread.

sentences.zh: 有司行之急，嬰穉輒棄擲。

translations.literal: The authorities enforced this harshly, and infants and small children were often abandoned and cast away.
translations.idiomatic: Local authorities enforced the policy harshly, and infants were often abandoned.

sentences.zh: 開心疏請四郊各定一村，移居者與屋宇聚處。

translations.literal: Kaixin memorialized requesting that one village be designated in each of the four suburbs, where those who moved would be housed together in dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Kaixin petitioned to designate a village in each suburban district where relocated families could be sheltered together.

sentences.zh: 旋又疏言：「立政之始，一事之得失，關天下萬世之利害。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again memorialized: "At the beginning of establishing government, the gain or loss of a single matter concerns the benefit and harm of the realm for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted another memorial: "At the outset of a new regime, the outcome of any single policy bears on the welfare of the realm for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不能盡陳，封章不敢頻瀆。

translations.literal: Memorials cannot fully set forth everything, and sealed submissions dare not be made frequently in importunity.
translations.idiomatic: Written memorials cannot convey everything, and I dare not burden Your Majesty with repeated submissions.

sentences.zh: 乞時賜召對，霽顏聽受。

translations.literal: I beg that I may from time to time be granted audience, with a serene countenance to receive my words.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be granted regular audiences, that Your Majesty may hear my counsel in person.

sentences.zh: 庶用人施政，悉奉宸斷。

translations.literal: Thus employment of men and conduct of government would all follow the emperor's own decisions.
translations.idiomatic: So that appointments and policies might all follow Your Majesty's own judgment."

sentences.zh: 」睿親王攝政，入朝，朝臣皆跪迎，開心疏請敕禮部詳定儀注。

translations.literal: " When the Prince Regent held the regency and entered court, all court officials knelt to welcome him; Kaixin memorialized requesting that the Ministry of Rites be ordered to set the ritual regulations in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Regent Dorgon attended court during the regency, all officials knelt to receive him; Kaixin petitioned for the Ministry of Rites to establish detailed court protocol.

sentences.zh: 江、浙、湖廣諸行省初定，開心疏請急置撫按，以時綏撫。

translations.literal: As the Jiangsu-Zhejiang and Huguang provinces were first pacified, Kaixin memorialized requesting urgent appointment of governors and censors to pacify them in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jiangnan, Zhejiang, and Huguang provinces were being pacified, Kaixin urged swift appointment of governors and censors to restore order.

sentences.zh: 並得旨俞允。

translations.literal: All received imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all these proposals.

sentences.zh: 擢左僉都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三年，坐事，罷。

translations.literal: In the third year, because of an offense, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1646 he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 八年，召起原官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was summoned back to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1651 he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 旋超擢左都御史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted over the usual steps to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted directly to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 開心子而抃，為唐王時舉人。

translations.literal: Kaixin's son Er Ban had been a provincial graduate under the Prince of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Kaixin's son Er Ban had obtained his provincial degree under the Prince of Tang during the Southern Ming.

sentences.zh: 九年，開心疏乞許而抃會試，禮部議不許，開心坐奪職，永不敘用。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Kaixin memorialized begging that Er Ban be permitted to take the metropolitan examination; the Ministry of Rites deliberated and did not permit it; Kaixin was stripped of office for this and permanently barred from appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1652 Kaixin petitioned to allow Er Ban to sit the metropolitan examination; when the Ministry of Rites refused, Kaixin was stripped of office and permanently barred from appointment.

sentences.zh: 十年，諭曰：「開心有直名，畀風憲重任。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, an edict said: "Kaixin has a reputation for forthrightness, and was given heavy responsibility in censorial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1653 the emperor issued an edict: "Kaixin earned his reputation for integrity and was entrusted with important censorial duties.

sentences.zh: 不言國家大事，乃庇子瀆奏，辜朕望實深。

translations.literal: He did not speak of great matters of state, but shielded his son in an improper memorial—deeply betraying my hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Instead of addressing affairs of state, he abused his office to shield his son—a profound disappointment.

sentences.zh: 朕念開心大臣，一事差謬，遂永棄不用，心終未恝然。

translations.literal: I consider Kaixin a senior minister; for one error he was forever cast aside and not employed—my heart is still not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kaixin is a senior minister; to cast him aside permanently over one lapse still weighs on my conscience.

sentences.zh: 召還京。

translations.literal: Summon him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Recall him to the capital."

sentences.zh: 」開心至，疏論湖廣巡撫遲日益、偏沅巡撫金廷獻、鄖襄巡撫趙兆麟所屬寇盜充斥，剿撫無能。

translations.literal: " When Kaixin arrived, he memorialized criticizing Huguang governor Chi Riyi, Bianyuan governor Jin Tingxian, and Yunxiang governor Zhao Zhaolin: under their jurisdictions bandits and robbers filled the land, and suppression and pacification were ineffective.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return, Kaixin submitted memorials charging that bandits ran rampant under Huguang governor Chi Riyi, Bianyuan governor Jin Tingxian, and Yunxiang governor Zhao Zhaolin, who had proved unable to suppress or pacify them.

sentences.zh: 得旨，下部察議。

translations.literal: An edict was received, and the matter was sent to the ministries for investigation and deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministries to investigate.

sentences.zh: 又言：「江南諸行省，每因捕治叛逆，株連無辜。

translations.literal: He also said: "In the Jiangnan provinces, in capturing and punishing rebels, the innocent are often implicated.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "In the Jiangnan provinces, efforts to capture rebels often ensnare the innocent.

sentences.zh: 如常鎮紳士王期升、路邁、蔣拱辰等，久錮獄中，虛實未辨。

translations.literal: Such as the gentry Wang Qisheng, Lu Mai, and Jiang Gongchen of Chang Prefecture, long imprisoned, with guilt or innocence still undetermined.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry such as Wang Qisheng, Lu Mai, and Jiang Gongchen of Changzhou have languished in prison with their cases unresolved.

sentences.zh: 就一方一事，可推之他省。

translations.literal: From one region and one matter, this can be extended to other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: What holds in one place surely holds elsewhere as well."

sentences.zh: 」上命確察以聞。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered thorough investigation and report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a thorough investigation and report.

sentences.zh: 時方考察京官，甄別翰林，開心疏論大學士馮銓、陳名夏等，各植門戶，開朋黨之漸，上命開心據實覆奏，未能實指其人，得旨申飭。

translations.literal: At the time the capital officials were being evaluated and Hanlin members screened; Kaixin memorialized criticizing grand secretaries Feng Quan, Chen Mingxia, and others for each establishing factions and opening the way to clique formation; the emperor ordered Kaixin to reply with facts; unable to identify any person specifically, he received an edict of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: During the evaluation of capital officials and screening of Hanlin scholars, Kaixin accused grand secretaries Feng Quan and Chen Mingxia of faction-building; when ordered to substantiate his charges, he could identify no specific individuals and received an imperial reprimand.

sentences.zh: 旋授原官。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He was shortly restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 十一年，疏陳時政，請禦經筵，親奏對，遴賢才，原過誤，許流徙自贖，重法司職掌。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he memorialized on current policies, requesting lectures before the emperor, personal audience, selection of worthy talent, pardon for errors, permission for exiles to redeem themselves, and emphasis on the judiciary's duties.
translations.idiomatic: In 1654 he submitted a comprehensive policy memorial calling for imperial lectures, direct audiences, selection of talent, forgiveness of past errors, self-redemption for exiles, and strengthened judicial authority.

sentences.zh: 上以疏中有「屏斥畋遊」語，諭曰：「講武習兵，乃祖宗立國大法，何謂畋遊？

translations.literal: Because the memorial contained the phrase "banish hunting excursions," an edict said: "Military drilling and martial exercises are the great law by which our ancestors founded the dynasty—what do you call hunting excursions?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took exception to the phrase "banish hunting and military outings," responding: "Military drill is the founding principle of our dynasty—how dare you call it frivolous diversion?

sentences.zh: 開心常談淺見，沽名塞責，殊負委任。

translations.literal: Kaixin constantly offers shallow views, seeking reputation while shirking responsibility—deeply failing the trust placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: Kaixin's shallow opinions and grandstanding have betrayed the trust placed in him.

sentences.zh: 」尋以名夏獲罪，責言官不先事舉發，降補太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: " Soon, when Mingxia was found guilty, censorial officials were blamed for not having exposed the matter beforehand, and he was demoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Mingxia was later condemned, censorial officials were blamed for failing to expose him beforehand, and Kaixin was demoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was transferred to vice minister of the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1655 he was transferred to vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「畿甸流民載道，有司恐誤留逃人，聽其轉徙。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In the capital region refugees fill the roads; local officials, fearing they may mistakenly retain fugitive laborers, allow them to wander on.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Refugees fill the roads around the capital; local officials, fearing they might harbor fugitive laborers, simply let them wander on.

sentences.zh: 請暫寬隱匿逃人之罪，以免株連，俾流民得邀撫輯。

translations.literal: I request temporarily easing the crime of concealing fugitive laborers to avoid implication by association, so that refugees may receive relief and settlement.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that penalties for concealing fugitive laborers be temporarily eased, so refugees may be settled rather than driven away."

sentences.zh: 」諭曰：「逃人之多，因有隱匿者，故立法不得不嚴，何謂株連？

translations.literal: " An edict said: "The great number of fugitive laborers is because there are those who conceal them; therefore the law must be strict—what do you call implication by association?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Laborers flee because others hide them—the law must be strict. What do you mean by 'implication'?

sentences.zh: 」因責開心沽譽，降補太僕寺寺丞。

translations.literal: " Accordingly Kaixin was blamed for currying reputation and demoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Kaixin was accused of grandstanding and demoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 尋擢少卿，協理兵部督捕事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to junior director and assigned to assist the Ministry of War in supervising capture operations.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to junior director and assigned to assist the Ministry of War in manhunt operations.

sentences.zh: 十三年，上以逃人多不獲，所司督責不嚴，复降補鴻臚寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, because many fugitive laborers were not captured and the responsible offices were not strictly supervising, he was again demoted to junior director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: In 1656, when fugitive laborers continued to evade capture, he was demoted again to junior director of the Court of State Ceremonial for insufficient supervision.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷太僕寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was transferred to junior director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In 1659 he was transferred to junior director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，擢總督倉場戶部侍郎，加工部尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, he was promoted to vice minister of Revenue supervising the grain granaries, with the nominal rank of minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1662 he was promoted to vice minister of Revenue overseeing the grain granaries, with the nominal rank of minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: =楊義=楊義，山西洪洞人。

translations.literal: =Yang Yi= Yang Yi, native of Hongdong, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi came from Hongdong in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，官山東聊城知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the Ming Chongzhen reign, he served as magistrate of Liaocheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: A Chongzhen-era jinshi, he served as magistrate of Liaocheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，授河南汝陽知縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of Ruyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1644 he was appointed magistrate of Ruyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 五年，行取，擢江西道御史，巡視兩浙鹽政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, selected by merit, he was promoted to censor of the Jiangxi circuit and assigned to inspect the salt administration of the two Zhejiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1648 he was selected for promotion to censor of the Jiangxi circuit and assigned to inspect salt administration in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 義疏請定行鹽掣驗之法，遴選清廉有司照引盤驗，御史親臨監掣。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized requesting establishment of regulations for inspection and verification of salt transport, selection of incorrupt officials to verify by tally against permits, with the censor personally supervising the inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Yi petitioned for standardized salt transport inspections, with honest officials verifying shipments against permits under the censor's personal supervision.

sentences.zh: 八年，睿親王得罪，義劾工部侍郎李迎晙前官營繕郎中，監造王府，僭擬禁廷，不數年閒，躐昇華膴，請敕部治罪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Prince Regent fell from grace, Yi impeached Li Yingjun, vice minister of Works, who when previously director of construction in the construction bureau had supervised the building of a princely mansion in imitation of forbidden palace standards and within a few years had leaped to lofty emoluments; he requested that the ministry be ordered to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1651, after Prince Regent Dorgon's fall, Yi impeached vice minister of Works Li Yingjun for having overseen construction of a princely mansion that imitated imperial palace standards during his earlier service, then vaulted to high office within years; he asked that Li be punished.

sentences.zh: 以迎晙事在赦前，寢其議。

translations.literal: Because Yingjun's offense occurred before an amnesty, the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The case was dropped because Li's offenses predated a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 复巡視長蘆鹽政，劾運使趙秉樞貪酷骫法，削籍逮治。

translations.literal: Again inspecting the Changlu salt administration, he impeached transport commissioner Zhao Bingshu for greed, cruelty, and bending the law; his name was struck from registers and he was arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the Changlu salt administration, he impeached transport commissioner Zhao Bingshu for corruption and abuse of law; Zhao was stripped of rank and arrested.

sentences.zh: 九年，督學江南，尋掌京畿道事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he served as educational commissioner of Jiangnan; soon afterward he took charge of the capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1652 he served as educational commissioner of Jiangnan, then took charge of the metropolitan circuit.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大學士陳名夏得罪，義因劾請告侍郎孫承澤黨附名夏，下部，令承澤休致。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when grand secretary Chen Mingxia was found guilty, Yi also impeached vice minister Sun Chengze, who had requested leave, for clinging to Mingxia's faction; the case was sent to the ministries, and Chengze was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In 1654, after Chen Mingxia's condemnation, Yi also impeached vice minister Sun Chengze for factional allegiance to Chen; Sun was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書劉正宗薦降調員外郎董國祥，擬授文選司郎中，義面詰正宗專擅，即具疏劾之，正宗得旨察議，國祥卒以贓敗，謫徙尚陽堡。

translations.literal: Personnel Minister Liu Zhengzong recommended demoted vice director Dong Guoxiang for appointment as director of the Bureau of Appointments; Yi confronted Zhengzong face to face for acting on his own authority and immediately submitted a memorial impeaching him; Zhengzong received an edict for investigation; Guoxiang was eventually exposed for corruption and banished to Shangyang Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When Personnel Minister Liu Zhengzong recommended demoted official Dong Guoxiang for a bureau directorship, Yi publicly challenged Liu's overreach and immediately impeached him; Dong was eventually exposed for corruption and exiled to Shangyang Fort.

sentences.zh: 十二年，條陳時政，言：「大學士呂宮久疾曠職，宜令歸田，養大臣廉恥。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he submitted items on current policies, saying: "Grand Secretary Lü Gong has long been ill and absent from duties; he should be ordered to retire to his fields and preserve the integrity of a senior minister.
translations.idiomatic: In 1655 he submitted a policy memorial arguing that long-ailing Grand Secretary Lü Gong should retire to preserve ministerial dignity.

sentences.zh: 」「巡按既停閱城、審錄諸事，督撫按期巡行，宜令簡隨從，慎關防，毋以擾民。

translations.literal: " "Since circuit censors have ceased city inspections and trial review, governors should simplify their retinues when making periodic rounds, guard against security breaches, and not disturb the people.
translations.idiomatic: With circuit censors no longer conducting city inspections, he urged governors to travel with smaller retinues and avoid harassing the populace.

sentences.zh: 」「兵民匱乏，請令各州縣禀生捐銀準貢，以給滿洲兵備鞍馬器用，餘賑被災貧民。

translations.literal: " "Soldiers and commoners are destitute; I request that licentiates in each prefecture and county be permitted to donate silver for quasi-gongshi status, to supply Manchu troops with saddles, horses, and equipment, with the remainder to relief disaster-stricken poor.
translations.idiomatic: To relieve hardship among soldiers and civilians, he proposed allowing licentiates to purchase quasi-gongshi status, with funds supplying Manchu troops' equipment and relief for disaster victims.

sentences.zh: 」「諭旨嚴禁加派，有司抗不遵行。

translations.literal: " "Edicts strictly forbid additional levies, but officials defy them.
translations.idiomatic: Despite edicts banning extra levies, officials continued to impose them.

sentences.zh: 如臣籍洪洞，地畝正糧外，又加驛站坐司馬夫、工食、公費等項，幾半正糧。

translations.literal: In my native Hongdong, beyond regular land tax, additions for postal stations, stable attendants, labor provisions, and public expenses nearly equal half the regular tax.
translations.idiomatic: In my native Hongdong, surcharges for postal stations, stable hands, labor, and public expenses nearly equaled half the regular land tax.

sentences.zh: 祈敕禁革。

translations.literal: I pray that an edict order their abolition.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that these be abolished by imperial edict."

sentences.zh: 」會宮已得旨致仕，飭下所司議行。

translations.literal: " As Lü had already received edict to retire, the ministries were ordered to deliberate and implement.
translations.idiomatic: Lü had already retired by edict; the other proposals were referred to the ministries.

sentences.zh: 時議復設巡按，義奏請甄舉才守兼優考試，請簡不拘資俸。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of restoring circuit censors; Yi memorialized requesting selection by examination of those excellent in both talent and integrity, with recommendations not bound by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: When debate arose over restoring circuit censors, Yi argued they should be selected by examination for combined talent and integrity, without seniority restrictions.

sentences.zh: 是歲四遷至刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: That year, through four transfers he reached vice minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: That year he rose through four promotions to vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十四年，調工部。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was transferred to the Works Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1657 he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 十七年，調倉場侍郎，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was transferred to vice minister of the granaries and promoted to minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1660 he was transferred to granary vice minister and promoted to minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In 1662 he retired.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: =林起龍=林起龍，順天大興人。

translations.literal: =Lin Qilong= Lin Qilong, native of Daxing, Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Qilong came from Daxing in Shuntian (Beijing).

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1646, he was appointed supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 疏請嚴禁白蓮、大成、混元、無為等邪教。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting strict prohibition of the White Lotus, Dacheng, Hunyuan, Wuwei, and other heterodox sects.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for strict suppression of White Lotus, Dacheng, Hunyuan, Wuwei, and other banned sects.

sentences.zh: 又疏請重守令，課以十五事，曰：招流亡，墾荒萊，巡阡陌，勸樹藝，稽戶口，均賦稅，輕徭役，除盜賊，抑豪強，懲衙蠹，賑災患，濟孤寡，濬溝池，治橋樑，興學校。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting emphasis on prefects and magistrates, assessing them on fifteen items, namely: recruiting refugees, reclaiming wasteland, inspecting fields, encouraging planting, checking household registers, equalizing taxes, lightening corvée, eliminating bandits, restraining the powerful, punishing yamen parasites, relieving disasters, aiding orphans and widows, dredging canals, repairing bridges, and establishing schools.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed holding prefects and magistrates accountable to fifteen duties: resettling refugees, reclaiming wasteland, inspecting fields, promoting agriculture, verifying household registers, equalizing taxes, reducing corvée, suppressing banditry, curbing local strongmen, punishing corrupt clerks, disaster relief, aid to orphans and widows, dredging canals, repairing bridges, and promoting schools.

sentences.zh: 考其殿最，而大吏以時訪察。

translations.literal: Their performance would be graded, and superior officials would inspect them on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Their performance would be graded through periodic inspection by superiors.

sentences.zh: 俱如所奏行。

translations.literal: All were implemented as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved all these proposals.

sentences.zh: 四年，劾山東巡撫丁文盛不能弭盜，並薦大理寺卿王永吉可代，部議以起龍有私，降二級外用。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he impeached Shandong governor Ding Wensheng for inability to quell bandits and also recommended Court of Review minister Wang Yongji as replacement; the ministries deliberated that Qilong had personal motives and demoted him two ranks for outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1647 he impeached Shandong governor Ding Wensheng for failing to quell banditry and recommended Court of Review minister Wang Yongji as replacement; the ministries ruled Qilong acted from personal motive and demoted him two ranks for outside service.

sentences.zh: 又坐劾登州道楊雲鶴婪贓不實，奪官。

translations.literal: He was also punished for impeaching Dengzhou intendant Yang Yunhe for greed and bribery without factual basis, and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later stripped of office for a baseless corruption charge against Dengzhou intendant Yang Yunhe.

sentences.zh: 世祖親政，召來京。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor personally assumed government, he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzhi took personal rule, Qilong was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十年，復原官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1653 he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅未靖，急轉餉，不遑言積貯，起龍請敕計臣籌畫，先實京倉，次及近輔各直省，務使倉有儲穀，備水旱，應調發。

translations.literal: At the time the armies were not yet pacified and grain transport was urgent, leaving no leisure to discuss reserves; Qilong requested that the planning minister be ordered to scheme: first fill the capital granaries, then those of nearby provinces, ensuring stores of grain for drought and flood and for dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: With armies still active and grain transport urgent, Qilong urged planners to first fill Beijing's granaries, then those of neighboring provinces, building reserves against drought, flood, and military needs.

sentences.zh: 又言：「滿洲兵昔在盛京，無餉而富；

translations.literal: He also said: "Manchu troops formerly at Mukden were rich without stipends;
translations.idiomatic: He also noted: "Manchu soldiers at Mukden prospered without stipends,

sentences.zh: 今在京師，有餉而貧。

translations.literal: now in the capital they are poor despite stipends.
translations.idiomatic: yet in Beijing they are poor despite receiving pay.

sentences.zh: 時地既迥異，法制宜更定。

translations.literal: Times and place being utterly different, regulations ought to be revised.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstances have changed entirely—the system must be revised.

sentences.zh: 凡駐守徵行，所需馬匹、草束、軍裝、戎器，悉動官帑籌備，毋使拮据。

translations.literal: For all garrison duty and campaigns, horses, fodder, military dress, and weapons needed should all be supplied from official coffers, not letting them be in straits.
translations.idiomatic: Horses, fodder, uniforms, and weapons for garrison and campaign duty should all come from state funds, sparing soldiers hardship."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，諭曰：「滿洲兵建功最多，資生無策，十年來未有言及此者。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, an edict said: "Manchu troops have achieved the most merit and have no means of livelihood; in ten years no one has spoken of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded: "Manchu soldiers have earned the most glory yet have no livelihood—no one has raised this in a decade.

sentences.zh: 起龍實心為國，忠誠可嘉！

translations.literal: Qilong's heart is sincere for the state—his loyalty is admirable!
translations.idiomatic: Qilong serves the state with genuine devotion—his loyalty is admirable!"

sentences.zh: 」下部議，以五品京堂用，起龍疏辭。

translations.literal: " The ministries were ordered to deliberate; he was to be employed as a fifth-rank capital official; Qilong memorialized declining.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries recommended him for fifth-rank capital appointment, but Qilong declined.

sentences.zh: 十一年，轉刑科，加大理寺寺丞銜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he transferred to the Punishments Section and was given the nominal rank of vice director of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1654 he transferred to the Punishments Section with the nominal rank of Court of Review vice director.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「州縣吏媚事上官，耗費不貲，請禁革；

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Prefectural and county clerks flatter superiors at great expense; I request this be prohibited;
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to ban the costly flattery prefectural and county clerks lavished on superiors;

sentences.zh: 並請遣廉能大臣巡行各直省，體察利弊。

translations.literal: and I request dispatch of honest and capable ministers to tour all provinces and assess benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: and to dispatch honest, capable ministers to tour the provinces and assess local conditions.

sentences.zh: 」既，疏劾總河楊方興及工部尚書劉昌，召方興、昌相質，所劾皆不實，部議當杖流，上特宥之，左授光祿寺署正。

translations.literal: " Thereafter he memorialized impeaching Grand Canal director-general Yang Fangxing and Works Minister Liu Chang; Fangxing and Chang were summoned to confront the charges; all impeachments proved unfounded; the ministries recommended beating and exile; the emperor specially pardoned him and demoted him to acting director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Grand Canal director Yang Fangxing and Works Minister Liu Chang; when both men were summoned to answer the charges, every accusation proved false; though the ministries recommended beating and exile, the emperor pardoned him and demoted him to acting director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷大理寺寺丞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1655 he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 十三年，一歲中三遷，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, through three transfers within one year, he was promoted to vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1656 he rose through three promotions in a single year to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十五年，改戶部侍郎，總督倉場。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was transferred to vice minister of Revenue and appointed to supervise the grain granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1658 he became vice minister of Revenue overseeing the grain granaries.

sentences.zh: 十六年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1659 he received the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 疏請更定綠旗兵制，略言：「有制之師，兵雖少，一以當十，餉愈省、兵愈強而國富；

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting revision of the Green Banner army system, stating in summary: "A disciplined army, though few in number, each man counts for ten; pay is more economical, troops stronger, and the state richer;
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for reform of the Green Banner army system, arguing: "A disciplined force, though small, fights tenfold; pay costs less, soldiers fight harder, and the state grows richer;

sentences.zh: 無制之師，兵雖多，萬不敵千，餉愈費、兵愈弱而國貧。

translations.literal: an undisciplined army, though many in number, ten thousand cannot match one thousand; pay is more costly, troops weaker, and the state poorer.
translations.idiomatic: an undisciplined force, though large, ten thousand cannot match one thousand; pay costs more, soldiers fight worse, and the state grows poorer.

sentences.zh: 今綠營兵幾六十萬，而地方有事，即請滿洲大兵，雖多仍不足用。

translations.literal: Today Green Banner troops number nearly six hundred thousand, yet when the regions have trouble, Manchu banner troops are immediately requested; though many, they are still insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Green Banner forces number nearly six hundred thousand, yet whenever trouble arises the court must call on Manchu banner troops—numbers alone are not enough.

sentences.zh: 推原其故，總緣將官赴任，召募家丁，隨營開糧，軍牢、伴當、吹手、轎夫，皆充兵數。

translations.literal: Tracing the root cause, it is entirely because when generals take up posts they recruit household retainers, who draw rations with the camp; military runners, attendants, trumpeters, and sedan-bearers all count as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The root cause is that generals recruit personal retainers who draw camp rations—runners, attendants, trumpeters, and sedan-bearers all count toward troop strength.

sentences.zh: 甚有地方鋪戶子侄，充兵免徭。

translations.literal: Some even have sons and nephews of local shopkeepers enrolled as soldiers to escape corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Some local shopkeepers' sons and nephews even enlist as soldiers simply to escape corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 其月餉則歸之本管，馬兵剋扣草料，驛遞缺馬，亦供營兵應付。

translations.literal: Their monthly pay goes to their commanding officer; cavalrymen have fodder deducted; when courier stations lack horses, camp soldiers are also supplied to meet the need.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly pay goes to commanding officers; cavalry fodder is skimmed; when courier stations lack horses, camp soldiers are pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 是以馬皆骨立，鞭策不前。

translations.literal: Thus horses are all skin and bones, and the whip cannot drive them forward.
translations.idiomatic: Horses are reduced to skin and bone and cannot be driven forward.

sentences.zh: 又如弓箭、刀槍、盔甲、火器，俱鈍弊朽壞，帳房、窩鋪、雨衣、弓箭罩，則竟闕不具。

translations.literal: Again, bows, arrows, swords, spears, armor, and firearms are all dull, worn out, and rotten; tents, shelters, rain capes, and bow covers are entirely missing.
translations.idiomatic: Bows, blades, armor, and firearms are dull and broken; tents, shelters, rain capes, and bow covers are entirely lacking.

sentences.zh: 春秋兩操，不復舉行。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn drills are no longer conducted.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn drills are no longer held.

sentences.zh: 將不知分合奇正之勢，兵不知坐作進退之法。

translations.literal: Generals do not know the disposition of combined and divided forces or orthodox and unorthodox tactics; soldiers do not know the methods of sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating.
translations.idiomatic: Generals know nothing of combined maneuvers or tactical variation; soldiers know nothing of drill and formation.

sentences.zh: 徒空國帑，竭民膏，雖★何益？

translations.literal: They merely empty the state treasury and exhaust the people's substance—what use though [many]?
translations.idiomatic: They merely drain the treasury and exhaust the people—of what use are they?

sentences.zh: 推其病有二：一則營兵原以戡亂，今乃責之捕盜；

translations.literal: Tracing its ailments, there are two: first, camp soldiers were originally for suppressing rebellion, but now they are charged with catching bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Two ailments lie at the root: first, camp soldiers were meant to suppress rebellion, yet are now tasked with catching bandits;

sentences.zh: 一則出餉養兵，原以備戰守之用，今則加以剋扣。

translations.literal: second, pay is issued to maintain troops for war and defense, but now it is subject to deductions.
translations.idiomatic: second, pay was meant to sustain soldiers for war and defense, yet is now systematically skimmed.

sentences.zh: 兵丁所得，僅能存活，又不按月支發，貧乏何以自支？

translations.literal: What soldiers receive barely keeps them alive, and it is not paid monthly—how can the destitute support themselves?
translations.idiomatic: What soldiers receive barely keeps them alive, and pay is not issued on schedule—how can the destitute survive?

sentences.zh: 今誠抽練綠旗精兵二十萬，養以四十萬之餉，餉厚兵精，地方有警，戰守有人。

translations.literal: If we now truly select and drill two hundred thousand elite Green Banner troops, maintaining them on four hundred thousand taels of pay, with generous pay and elite troops, when the regions have alarms there will be men for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: If we selected and drilled two hundred thousand elite Green Banner troops, paying them well from a budget of four hundred thousand taels, the regions would have capable defenders whenever trouble arose.

sentences.zh: 不過十年，可使庫藏充溢。

translations.literal: Within no more than ten years, the treasury could be filled to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years the treasury would overflow.

sentences.zh: 」下所司議行。

translations.literal: " The responsible offices were ordered to deliberate and implement.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the ministries for implementation.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加太子太保、兵部尚書，巡撫鳳陽。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was given the additional titles of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and minister of War, and appointed governor of Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1660 he received the titles of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and minister of War and was appointed governor of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 時議懲官吏犯贓，視輕重科罪，不許納贖，起龍疏請如舊例收贖充餉，下廷議，請從之。

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed to punish corrupt officials according to severity without permitting redemption; Qilong memorialized requesting collection of redemption fees as in the old precedent to supplement military pay; the matter was sent to court deliberation, which recommended approval.
translations.idiomatic: When the court proposed punishing corrupt officials without allowing redemption, Qilong petitioned to restore the old practice of collecting redemption fees for military pay; court deliberation recommended approval.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「立法止貪，今因濟餉而貸法，如民生何？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Laws were made to stop corruption; now to supply pay we waive the law—what of the people's livelihood?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Laws exist to stop corruption—how can we waive them to fund the army? What of the people's welfare?

sentences.zh: 」絀起龍議不行。

translations.literal: " Qilong's proposal was rejected and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Qilong's proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，授起龍漕運總督，迭疏請免濱海移民田地賦額，濬淮城迤南運河，直達射陽湖，修築濟寧、臨清諸處堤閘，並請禁運丁毋病民，運弁毋病丁，條議以上，皆從其請。

translations.literal: When the Sage Ancestor took the throne, Qilong was appointed director-general of grain transport; in successive memorials he requested exemption of tax quotas on coastal resettlement lands, dredging of the canal south of Huai City directly to Sheyang Lake, repair of dikes and sluices at Jining, Linqing, and other places, and prohibition of transport laborers harming the people and transport officers harming the laborers; all proposals submitted were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Kangxi ascended the throne, Qilong was appointed director-general of grain transport; he petitioned repeatedly to exempt coastal resettlement lands from tax, dredge the canal south of Huai City to Sheyang Lake, repair dikes and sluices at Jining and Linqing, and protect transport workers and civilians from abuse—all approved.

sentences.zh: 又疏請禁運丁多攜貨物，稽滯漕運，定分地稽察例。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting prohibition of transport laborers carrying excessive goods, which delayed grain transport, and establishment of regulations for territorial inspection.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to ban transport workers from carrying excess cargo that delayed grain shipments, establishing territorial inspection rules.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，糧艘至濟寧，運丁有多攜貨物者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, when grain barges reached Jining, many transport laborers were carrying excessive goods.
translations.idiomatic: In 1667, when grain barges reached Jining, many transport workers were found carrying excess cargo.

sentences.zh: 事覺，總河盧崇峻疏陳起龍言江南漕儲道既裁，總漕不任稽察，御史張志尹糾起龍不引罪。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, Grand Canal director Lu Chongjun memorialized stating that Qilong had said the Jiangnan grain storage circuit had been abolished and the transport director-general could not bear inspection duties; censor Zhang Zhiyin impeached Qilong for not accepting guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter surfaced, Grand Canal director Lu Chongjun reported that Qilong had claimed the Jiangnan grain storage post was abolished and he could not supervise inspections; censor Zhang Zhiyin impeached Qilong for failing to accept responsibility.

sentences.zh: 上以詰起龍，起龍謝失職，鐫三級休致。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Qilong; Qilong acknowledged dereliction of duty and was reduced three ranks and ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Qilong, who acknowledged dereliction of duty; he was reduced three ranks and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，仁宗親政，閱世祖實錄，得起龍更定綠營兵制疏，諭諸行省督撫整飭營伍，並以所言抽練精兵，是否可仿行，飭妥議具奏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, when Emperor Renzong personally assumed government, reading the Veritable Records of Shizu, he found Qilong's memorial on revising the Green Banner army system; he ordered governors in all provinces to rectify the camps, and also whether the proposed selection and drilling of elite troops could be imitated, ordering careful deliberation and memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799, when Emperor Jiaqing took personal rule, he found Qilong's memorial on Green Banner reform while reading Shunzhi's veritable records; he ordered provincial governors to rectify the camps and deliberate whether Qilong's plan for elite troop selection could be adopted.

sentences.zh: 諸行省督撫憚改作，議格不行。

translations.literal: Governors in all provinces feared reform and blocked the proposal from implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors, fearing reform, blocked the proposal.

sentences.zh: =硃克簡=硃克簡，字敬可，江南寶應人。

translations.literal: =Zhu Kejian= Zhu Kejian, style Jingke, native of Baoying, Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kejian, whose style was Jingke, came from Baoying in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治四年進士，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1647, he was appointed Grand Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 五年，考授御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, through examination he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1648 he passed examination and was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 八年，典廣東鄉試。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he presided over the Guangdong provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1651 he served as chief examiner for the Guangdong provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 十二年，巡按福建。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he served as circuit censor of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1655 he was appointed circuit censor of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 福建八府一州，其五濱海。

translations.literal: Fujian has eight prefectures and one department; five of them border the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian had eight prefectures and one department, five of them coastal.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功時入寇，民苦焚掠。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong frequently raided, and the people suffered burning and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong raided repeatedly, and the people suffered burning and plunder.

sentences.zh: 克簡至，申明軍政，綢繆防禦，請增兵防仙霞關。

translations.literal: When Kejian arrived, he clarified military administration, made thorough defensive preparations, and requested additional troops to guard Xianxia Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival Kejian tightened military administration, strengthened defenses, and requested additional troops for Xianxia Pass.

sentences.zh: 時兵部尚書王永吉疏請減兵額，汰營兵老弱，下諸行省。

translations.literal: At the time War Minister Wang Yongji memorialized requesting reduction of troop quotas and elimination of aged and weak camp soldiers; the order was sent to all provinces.
translations.idiomatic: War Minister Wang Yongji had petitioned to cut troop quotas and eliminate aged and weak camp soldiers; the order went to all provinces.

sentences.zh: 克簡疏言：「福建內防山賊，外禦海寇，省兵三萬四千，不可復減。

translations.literal: Kejian memorialized: "Fujian defends against mountain bandits within and sea raiders without; provincial troops number thirty-four thousand and cannot be further reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian argued: "Fujian must defend against mountain bandits inland and sea raiders on the coast; its thirty-four thousand provincial troops cannot be cut further.

sentences.zh: 」上如其議。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又疏論防海，略言：「用水師不難得其力，難得其心。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on coastal defense, stating in summary: "Using the navy, it is not hard to obtain their labor, but hard to win their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on coastal defense: "It is easy to command the navy's labor but hard to win its loyalty.

sentences.zh: 漳泉為鄭成功故土，沿海多戚屬，宜以連保法察其踪跡，考​​其身家，不使入伍；

translations.literal: Zhangzhou and Quanzhou are Zheng Chenggong's homeland; along the coast there are many kinsmen; the mutual-guarantee system should be used to track their movements and examine their backgrounds, not permitting them to enlist;
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou and Quanzhou were Zheng Chenggong's homeland, and many coastal residents were his kinsmen; mutual-guarantee groups should track their movements and bar them from enlistment;

sentences.zh: 降者令歸耕，或移置他軍，使離舊巢，乃堅歸志。

translations.literal: those who surrender should be ordered to return to farming, or transferred to other armies, removed from old nests, so their resolve to submit is firm.
translations.idiomatic: surrendered men should return to farming or be transferred to other units, removed from old haunts, to firm their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 水師戰海中，破浪擒賊，當受上賞，宜著為令。

translations.literal: When the navy fights at sea, breaking waves and capturing bandits, they should receive highest reward; this should be established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Naval victories at sea deserve the highest rewards—this should be written into law.

sentences.zh: 水師用在舟，木、竹、釘鐵、油、麻、★葉，皆海之所無，一物不具，不可以為舟。

translations.literal: The navy depends on vessels; wood, bamboo, nails, iron, oil, hemp, and [palm] leaves—all absent at sea—if one item is lacking, a vessel cannot be made.
translations.idiomatic: The navy depends on ships, and wood, bamboo, nails, iron, oil, hemp, and palm leaves—none found at sea—must all be supplied; one missing item means no ship can be built.

sentences.zh: 宜設專官譏察，毋以資敵。

translations.literal: Special officers for inspection should be established, not supplying the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Special inspectors should be appointed to prevent supplies reaching the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」「寧化、崇安濱海要地，今俱為賊踞，當按形勢增兵固守。

translations.literal: " "Ninghua and Chong'an are key coastal places, now all occupied by bandits; troops should be increased according to terrain and firmly held.
translations.idiomatic: Ninghua and Chong'an, key coastal positions now held by rebels, should receive reinforced garrisons according to terrain."

sentences.zh: 」又立六規二十四約，與提督馬成功、總兵王之綱等深相結納，諸將咸奉令。

translations.literal: " He also established six regulations and twenty-four covenants, formed deep alliances with regional commander Ma Chenggong, commander-in-chief Wang Zhigang, and others, and all generals obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: He also established six regulations and twenty-four covenants, forged close ties with regional commander Ma Chenggong and commander-in-chief Wang Zhigang, and won obedience from all generals.

sentences.zh: 巡汀州，聞成功兵攻福州，即率汀州鎮兵還援。

translations.literal: While inspecting Tingzhou, hearing that Chenggong's troops were attacking Fuzhou, he immediately led Tingzhou garrison troops back to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: While touring Tingzhou, he heard Zheng Chenggong was attacking Fuzhou and immediately led Tingzhou garrison troops to reinforce the city.

sentences.zh: 成功兵引退，克簡入城，曰：「寇知我援寡，且復來。

translations.literal: Chenggong's troops withdrew; Kejian entered the city and said: "The bandits know our reinforcements are few and will come again.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's troops withdrew; Kejian entered the city and said, "The enemy knows our reinforcements are thin and will return.

sentences.zh: 」令完城垣、簡卒伍為備。

translations.literal: " He ordered completion of city walls and selection of troops for preparation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the walls repaired and troops readied for defense.

sentences.zh: 數日，成功兵復至。

translations.literal: Within days, Chenggong's troops returned.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Zheng's forces returned.

sentences.zh: 初，官軍得成功兵輒誅之，克簡令發不過五寸者貸死，編為民，得萬餘人，皆恩克簡，至是助守城，發★擊寇，寇潰，遂出戰，解圍去。

translations.literal: Initially, when government troops captured Chenggong's soldiers they always executed them; Kejian ordered that those under five chi in height be spared death and enrolled as civilians, obtaining more than ten thousand men, all grateful to Kejian; at this time they helped defend the city, fired [cannon] at the bandits; the bandits broke; then they went out to battle and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Previously government troops executed every Zheng soldier they captured; Kejian spared those under five chi tall, enrolling more than ten thousand as civilians who gratefully helped defend the city; they fired cannon at the invaders, who broke and fled, and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 至漳州，布政使詳請徵逋賦，克簡力阻之，疏請蠲徵，上從之。

translations.literal: Arriving at Zhangzhou, the provincial administration commissioner detailed a request to collect overdue taxes; Kejian strongly blocked it and memorialized requesting exemption; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhangzhou, when the provincial administration commissioner proposed collecting overdue taxes, Kejian blocked the plan and petitioned for exemption; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 至福清，以閩安地當衝，設兵守之，連江、羅源、福清、長樂諸縣要隘皆置汛。

translations.literal: Arriving at Fuqing, because Min'an was a strategic point, he stationed troops to guard it; key passes in Lianjiang, Luoyuan, Fuqing, and Changle counties all received garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuqing he garrisoned the strategic Min'an crossing and posted troops at key passes throughout Lianjiang, Luoyuan, Fuqing, and Changle.

sentences.zh: 至興化，見道有流民，與知府張彥珩議賑，活者萬數千人。

translations.literal: Arriving at Xinghua, seeing refugees on the roads, he discussed relief with prefect Zhang Yanheng, saving tens of thousands of lives.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinghua he found refugees on the roads; working with Prefect Zhang Yanheng on relief, he saved tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 至泉州，令崇武、獺戶、大盈諸隘皆置汛。

translations.literal: Arriving at Quanzhou, he ordered garrisons placed at Chongwu, Tahu, Daying, and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: At Quanzhou he posted garrisons at Chongwu, Tahu, Daying, and other strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 至延平，知其地舟人多通寇，令循江諸州縣設「循環簿」譏察。

translations.literal: Arriving at Yanping, knowing that boatmen there often communicated with bandits, he ordered river counties to establish "rotation registers" for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanping, where boatmen often colluded with rebels, he ordered river counties to keep rotation registers for inspection.

sentences.zh: 汀州、延平、建安三郡多伏戎，克簡遣兵破其巢穴，離其黨羽，次第皆就撫。

translations.literal: Tingzhou, Yanping, and Jian'an three prefectures had many hidden rebels; Kejian sent troops to destroy their nests and separate their followers; one after another they all submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In Tingzhou, Yanping, and Jian'an, where rebels lurked in numbers, Kejian sent troops to destroy their hideouts and break up their bands until all submitted.

sentences.zh: 迭疏請汰冗員，蠲鹽課，卹驛困，皆報可。

translations.literal: In successive memorials he requested elimination of redundant posts, exemption of salt levies, and relief for distressed courier stations; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned repeatedly to cut redundant posts, reduce salt levies, and relieve distressed courier stations—all approved.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，乞歸。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, he requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1693.

sentences.zh: 子約，以副貢生充教習，歷知福安、南豐、費諸縣，擢晉州，所至皆有惠政。

translations.literal: His son Yue, as a deputy tribute graduate serving as instructor, successively governed Fu'an, Nanfeng, and Fei counties, was promoted to Jin Prefecture, and everywhere he went enacted benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue, a deputy tribute graduate who served as instructor, governed Fu'an, Nanfeng, and Fei counties before promotion to Jin Prefecture, earning a reputation for benevolent rule everywhere he served.

sentences.zh: =成性=成性，字我存，江南和州人。

translations.literal: =Cheng Xing= Cheng Xing, style Wocun, native of Hezhou, Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xing, whose style was Wocun, came from Hezhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，授中書科中書。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed secretary of the Secretariat Section.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1649, he was appointed Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 十四年，考授御史，巡按福建。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, through examination he was appointed censor and served as circuit censor of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1657 he passed examination and was appointed circuit censor of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「福建山海征剿，師旅繁興，民窮地荒。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Fujian's mountain and sea campaigns and suppressions have brought frequent military activity; the people are destitute and the land desolate.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Fujian's mountain and coastal campaigns have brought constant military activity; the people are destitute and the land lies waste.

sentences.zh: 條上四策：一曰嚴汛守。

translations.literal: He submitted four policies in items: first, strict garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed four policies: first, strengthen garrison defense.

sentences.zh: 濱海地寥廓，不能遍防。

translations.literal: Coastal territory is vast and cannot be fully defended.
translations.idiomatic: The coastal territory is too vast to defend everywhere.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜設水師，求熟練舟楫、諳識水性之將吏，廣選舵工水手，繚椗招鬥，惟其能者，禀餉不為常格。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks a navy should be established, seeking officers skilled in boats and knowing water conditions, broadly selecting helmsmen and sailors, recruiting by ability in rope-work and combat, with rations not bound by regular standards.
translations.idiomatic: I propose establishing a navy, recruiting officers skilled in seamanship and sailors chosen for ability, paying them beyond standard rates.

sentences.zh: 以舟為家，銃械用其長技，操演習熟，庶幾水師可成。

translations.literal: Making vessels their home, using firearms according to their specialties, drilling until proficient—thus the navy may be formed.
translations.idiomatic: Living aboard their ships, using firearms to their strengths, and drilling until proficient—a navy could be built.

sentences.zh: 泉州近賊巢，水師宜移石湖。

translations.literal: Quanzhou is near the bandits' nest; the navy should be moved to Shihu.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhou lies near the rebel base; the navy should relocate to Shihu.

sentences.zh: 崇武、石芝駐陸軍為聲援。

translations.literal: Chongwu and Shizhi should station land forces as supporting presence.
translations.idiomatic: Land forces at Chongwu and Shizhi should serve as backup.

sentences.zh: 惠安北有峰尾司，宜駐兵，為惠州籓籬。

translations.literal: North of Hui'an is Fengwei Station; troops should be stationed there as a barrier for Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fengwei Station north of Hui'an should be garrisoned as a shield for Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 同安鄰廈門，當於高浦設屯，劉五店置警砲，時出遊騎巡視要隘。

translations.literal: Tong'an borders Xiamen; a garrison should be set at Gaopu, alarm guns placed at Liuwudian, and mounted patrols sent out periodically to inspect key passes.
translations.idiomatic: Tong'an borders Xiamen; a garrison at Gaopu, alarm guns at Liuwudian, and periodic cavalry patrols of key passes are needed.

sentences.zh: 此又惠州之脣齒也。

translations.literal: This is also the lip-and-teeth relationship for Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: These positions are likewise vital to Huizhou's defense.

sentences.zh: 一曰分界址。

translations.literal: Second, demarcating boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: Second, demarcate boundaries.

sentences.zh: 有司禁遏接濟，商阻物貴，民生窮蹙。

translations.literal: Officials prohibit and block supply; commerce is obstructed and goods are costly; the people's livelihood is strained.
translations.idiomatic: Official bans on supply have obstructed commerce, raised prices, and strained people's livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為先定禁例，若竹木、鑌鐵、硝磺、油、麻，毋許通貿。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks prohibitions should first be set: bamboo, timber, wrought iron, saltpeter, sulfur, oil, and hemp must not be traded.
translations.idiomatic: I propose clear prohibitions on trading bamboo, timber, wrought iron, saltpeter, sulfur, oil, and hemp.

sentences.zh: 小民日用所需，宜聽轉運。

translations.literal: Daily necessities of common people should be permitted for transport.
translations.idiomatic: Daily necessities should still be allowed through.

sentences.zh: 惟濱海大道或捷徑可通者，嚴立疆界。

translations.literal: Only along coastal highways or shortcuts that can connect, boundaries should be strictly established.
translations.idiomatic: Along coastal highways and shortcuts, boundaries should be strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 更定勾稽文法，以時比驗。

translations.literal: Audit regulations should be revised and verified on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Audit procedures should be revised and verified on schedule.

sentences.zh: 自泉州西出延平上游，去海甚遠，百貨交易，宜聽民便。

translations.literal: From Quanzhou west to the upper reaches of Yanping, far from the sea, trade in all goods should be left to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: From Quanzhou west to upper Yanping, far inland, trade should be left unrestricted.

sentences.zh: 一曰輯降眾。

translations.literal: Third, gathering surrendered masses.
translations.idiomatic: Third, manage surrendered populations.

sentences.zh: 山海嘯聚之徒，漸次來降。

translations.literal: Those who gathered in mountains and seas gradually came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain and coastal rebels have been surrendering in growing numbers.

sentences.zh: 入伍者多，歸耕者少。

translations.literal: Many enlisted in the army; few returned to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Too many enlist while too few return to farming.

sentences.zh: 間有悍氣未馴，凌轢鄉里。

translations.literal: Some with fierce temperament not yet tamed bully their villages.
translations.idiomatic: Some remain unruly and bully their neighbors.

sentences.zh: 居民亦負氣不相下，訐訟不受理，則自相格鬥。

translations.literal: Residents also hold fierce pride and will not yield; when accusations are not accepted for trial, they fight each other.
translations.idiomatic: Locals too refuse to back down; when courts reject their suits, they fight among themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜令解散宿怨，禁止羅織。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks they should be ordered to dissolve old grudges and prohibit fabricated accusations.
translations.idiomatic: I propose ordering old grudges dissolved and fabricated accusations banned.

sentences.zh: 新附之眾，合者漸分，聚者漸散，近者漸遠，庶可消弭反側。

translations.literal: Among newly submitted masses, those united should gradually separate, those gathered gradually disperse, those near gradually move far—thus unrest may be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Newly submitted groups should gradually be separated, dispersed, and relocated to eliminate unrest.

sentences.zh: 一曰清營伍。

translations.literal: Fourth, clearing the camp ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, clean up camp ranks.

sentences.zh: 府縣編氓，既有保甲，諸營什伍，猶未整齊。

translations.literal: Registered commoners in prefectures and counties already have mutual-responsibility groups, but camp squads and fives are still not organized.
translations.idiomatic: Registered civilians already have mutual-responsibility groups, but camp squads remain disorganized.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為當責成兵吏，自為版籍。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks military officers should be charged to compile their own registers.
translations.idiomatic: I propose holding military officers responsible for compiling their own registers.

sentences.zh: 略仿保甲之制，同居連坐。

translations.literal: Roughly imitating the mutual-responsibility system, those living together share liability.
translations.idiomatic: Following the mutual-responsibility model, cohabitants should share liability.

sentences.zh: 則軍伍肅、盜源遏矣。

translations.literal: Then the army ranks will be disciplined and the source of banditry checked.
translations.idiomatic: Then camp discipline would improve and banditry be checked at its source.

sentences.zh: 」事下兵部議行。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the Ministry of War for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of War for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 既，又上疏言：「下游四府濱海，海徼無險阻可守，且又兵力所不及。

translations.literal: Afterward, he again submitted a memorial stating: "The four downstream prefectures border the sea; the maritime frontier has no defensible terrain, and moreover lies beyond the reach of military strength.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted another memorial: "The four downstream prefectures lie on the coast. The maritime frontier has no natural defenses and lies beyond the army's reach.

sentences.zh: 宜令居民築土堡，多備長槍鳥銃，習為團練。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order residents to build earthen fortresses, prepare many long spears and arquebuses, and train in militia formations.
translations.idiomatic: Residents should be ordered to build earthen forts, stock long spears and arquebuses, and drill as militia.

sentences.zh: 賊至，人自為守，家自為戰，馳報附近將領，以兵赴援。

translations.literal: When bandits arrive, each person defends himself, each household fights for itself; they dispatch reports to nearby commanders, who send troops in relief.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits come, each man defends and each household fights; nearby commanders should be alerted to send relief.

sentences.zh: 久之使賊糧絕勢窮，未有不瓦解者也。

translations.literal: In time this will cut off the bandits' grain and exhaust their strength; none fail to disintegrate.
translations.idiomatic: In time the rebels' supplies would run dry and their strength fail—they would inevitably collapse.

sentences.zh: 」又疏論鹽場利弊，請裁上里、海口、牛田諸場，以福清知縣領其事。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized on the pros and cons of salt fields, requesting the abolition of the fields at Shangli, Haikou, and Niutian, with the magistrate of Fuqing put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he discussed salt-field administration, proposing to abolish the Shangli, Haikou, and Niutian fields and put the Fuqing magistrate in charge.

sentences.zh: 十六年，報績，授兵部主事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, his performance was reported and he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1659 his performance was reported and he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，始出就官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi, he finally left home to take office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1668 he finally returned to office.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授工科給事中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was appointed supervising secretary of the Public Works section.
translations.idiomatic: In 1672 he was appointed supervising secretary of the Public Works section.

sentences.zh: 時議招募遊民，開墾荒田。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of recruiting vagrants to open and cultivate wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: The court was debating whether to recruit vagrants to open wasteland.

sentences.zh: 性疏言：「民貧不能耕，乃有荒田。

translations.literal: Xing memorialized: "Because the people are poor and cannot farm, there is wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng submitted a memorial: "The people are too poor to farm—that is why land lies fallow.

sentences.zh: 遊民既失業，安能開墾？

translations.literal: Vagrants have already lost their livelihood—how can they open land?
translations.idiomatic: Vagrants have no livelihood—how can they reclaim wasteland?

sentences.zh: 請敕督撫令縣官勸民開墾，無力者上布政司給牛種貲錢。

translations.literal: He requested that governors and censors charge county officers to encourage the people to open land; those unable should report to the provincial treasurer for cattle, seed, and funds.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that governors order county magistrates to encourage reclamation, with the provincial treasurer supplying cattle, seed, and funds to those who could not afford them.

sentences.zh: 以本縣之民，墾本縣之田，官既易於稽察，朝廷本貲亦易於徵收。

translations.literal: Using the people of each county to cultivate the fields of that county, officials would find supervision easier and the court's seed funds easier to recover.
translations.idiomatic: Local people should reclaim local fields—easier for officials to supervise and for the court to recover its seed loans.

sentences.zh: 」又迭疏請獎進廉吏，為國家培元氣，密諭推舉督學，以重人才根本之地。

translations.literal: " He repeatedly memorialized asking to reward and promote upright officials, to nurture the state's vital force, with secret instructions to recommend educational commissioners, treating that post as the root of talent.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated memorials he called for promoting honest officials to restore the dynasty's vitality, and for secret instructions to elevate educational commissioners as the foundation of talent.

sentences.zh: 又疏陳民生十害，謂：「州縣胥役挾持長吏，為衙蠹之害；

translations.literal: He also memorialized the ten harms to the people's livelihood, saying: "Local clerks and runners hold the magistrate hostage—this is the harm of yamen parasites;
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted the ten harms afflicting common people: "County clerks who dominate their magistrates—yamen parasites;

sentences.zh: 官吏私交舊識，關說曲直，為抽豐之害；

translations.literal: Officials privately befriend old acquaintances and intercede to twist right and wrong—this is the harm of extortionate squeezing;
translations.idiomatic: Officials who pull strings for old friends and twist justice—the squeeze;

sentences.zh: 鄉民錢糧訟獄，必投在城所主之戶，聽其侵蝕唆使，為歇家之害；

translations.literal: Country people for tax, grain, and lawsuits must resort to host households in the city, who embezzle and instigate as they please—this is the harm of lodging brokers;
translations.idiomatic: Villagers who must rely on city lodging brokers for taxes and lawsuits, who skim and manipulate—broker harm;

sentences.zh: 大奸巨猾武斷鄉曲，為奸豪之害；

translations.literal: Great villains and scoundrels arbitrarily dominate the countryside—this is the harm of local tyrants;
translations.idiomatic: Powerful local bullies who rule the countryside—tyrants;

sentences.zh: 督撫及司道胥吏幹託有司，為上官胥吏之害；

translations.literal: Governors' and circuit intendants' clerks pull strings with subordinate officials—this is the harm of superior clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Clerks of governors and circuit officials who pull strings with subordinates—superior-clerk harm;

sentences.zh: 丞簿佐貳濫受訟牒，為佐貳之害；

translations.literal: Deputy magistrates indiscriminately accept lawsuit documents—this is the harm of auxiliary officials;
translations.idiomatic: Deputy magistrates who accept any lawsuit that comes their way—deputy harm;

sentences.zh: 奸民譸張上控，株連蔓衍，為越訴之害；

translations.literal: Cunning people fabricate and appeal upward; implicated parties spread and multiply—this is the harm of bypass appeals;
translations.idiomatic: Malicious litigants who fabricate charges and appeal upward, dragging in ever more people—bypass appeal;

sentences.zh: 顏料本色，緣時價低昂，不載由單，任意苛斂，為雜派之害；

translations.literal: Dyestuffs and tribute goods vary with market prices high and low, are not entered on the tax receipt, and are levied arbitrarily—this is the harm of miscellaneous surcharges;
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous levies on dyestuffs and tribute goods priced at whim rather than on the tax receipt—surcharge harm;

sentences.zh: 百姓十室九空，無藉乘急取利，逐月合券，俗謂'印子錢'，利至十之七八，折沒妻孥，為放債之害；

translations.literal: Nine of ten households among the people are empty; the destitute seize emergency to take profit, monthly contracts called 'stamp money' with interest reaching seven or eight tenths, forfeiting wives and children—this is the harm of usury;
translations.idiomatic: With nine of ten households ruined, predators lend 'stamp money' at seventy or eighty percent monthly interest, forfeiting wives and children—usury;

sentences.zh: 郵傳往來，強捉人夫，挽舟負輿，為縴夫之害。

translations.literal: Postal couriers going back and forth forcibly seize laborers to tow boats and carry sedan chairs—this is the harm of impressed transport workers.
translations.idiomatic: Postal traffic that impresses men to tow boats and carry sedan chairs—corvée harm.

sentences.zh: 請下所在有司，每季書狀，不蹈十害，申大吏按驗。

translations.literal: He requested that local officials each quarter submit written statements that they had not committed the ten harms, reported to senior officials for verification.
translations.idiomatic: He asked local officials to report quarterly that they had avoided the ten harms, subject to inspection by senior officials.

sentences.zh: 」又請飭督撫嚴飭所司，復社學，講鄉約，舉節孝，立義塚，不力行者，不得與卓異。

translations.literal: " He also requested that governors and censors strictly charge their subordinates to restore community schools, conduct village compacts, commend chastity and filial piety, and establish public burial grounds; those who did not earnestly implement these would not receive outstanding merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged governors to restore community schools, village compacts, chastity awards, and public graves—officials who failed to implement them would be denied outstanding evaluations.

sentences.zh: 旋擢掌科。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to chief supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to chief supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以疾乞歸，家居三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he begged leave for illness and returned home; after three years at home, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1676 he retired for illness, remained at home three years, and died.

sentences.zh: 國初循明舊，御史出為巡按。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, following Ming precedent, censors were dispatched as touring inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding, following Ming practice, censors were dispatched as touring inspectors.

sentences.zh: 順治七年罷，旋復設。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi year seven it was abolished, then soon re-established.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in 1650, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 八年，世祖親政，特敕誡諭，並命都察院察訪舉劾。

translations.literal: In year eight, the Shizu Emperor took personal rule, issued special edicts of admonition, and ordered the Censorate to investigate, report, and impeach.
translations.idiomatic: In 1651 the Shunzhi Emperor took direct rule, issued special instructions to touring censors, and charged the Censorate with investigation and impeachment.

sentences.zh: 禦太和殿，召新命諸巡按入見，賜坐宣諭。

translations.literal: He proceeded to the Hall of Supreme Harmony, summoned the newly appointed touring censors to audience, granted them seats, and announced his instructions.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hall of Supreme Harmony he summoned newly appointed touring censors, seated them, and delivered his instructions.

sentences.zh: 十七年，都察院復​​請罷，王大臣會議，安親王及侍郎石申等議留，別疏上。

translations.literal: In year seventeen, the Censorate again requested abolition; princes and ministers conferred; the Prince of An and Vice Minister Shi Shen and others argued for retention and submitted a separate memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In 1660 the Censorate again petitioned for abolition. At a princely conference the Prince of An and Vice Minister Shi Shen argued to keep the post and submitted a separate memorial.

sentences.zh: 又以御史陸光旭疏爭，令再議，仍議罷不復設。

translations.literal: Then censor Lu Guangxu memorialized in protest; they were ordered to deliberate again, and still decided on abolition with no re-establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lu Guangxu protested in a memorial; after further deliberation the court still decided to abolish the post permanently.

sentences.zh: 巡按能舉其職者，又有寧承勳按河南，請塞黃河決口；

translations.literal: Among touring censors who performed their duties well were Ning Chengxun, who inspected Henan and requested blocking the Yellow River breach;
translations.idiomatic: Notable touring censors included Ning Chengxun in Henan, who petitioned to seal the Yellow River breach;

sentences.zh: 秦世禎按江蘇，劾罷巡撫土國寶：最知名。

translations.literal: Qin Shizhen, who inspected Jiangsu and impeached Governor Tu Guobao—most famous.
translations.idiomatic: and Qin Shizhen in Jiangsu, who impeached and removed Governor Tu Guobao—the most famous case.

sentences.zh: 承勳大興人，明天啟舉人，自禮部主事考選御史，官至大理寺右寺正。

translations.literal: Chengxun was from Daxing; a Ming Tianqi juren; selected as censor from a Ministry of Rites principal clerk; he reached Right Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun was a Daxing native and Tianqi-era juren, promoted from Ministry of Rites clerk to censor, reaching Right Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 世禎自有傳。

translations.literal: Shizhen has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen has his own biography.

sentences.zh: =王命岳=王命岳，字伯諮，福建晉江人。

translations.literal: =Wang Mingyue= Wang Mingyue, style Bozi, native of Jinjiang, Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mingyue, whose style was Bozi, came from Jinjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of Shunzhi year twelve, appointed Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in 1655 and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 時雲南、貴州未定，策問及之。

translations.literal: At the time Yunnan and Guizhou were unsettled; the policy question touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan and Guizhou were still unconquered; the palace examination question addressed this.

sentences.zh: 命岳言：「李定國貳於孫可望，當緩定國，行間使與可望相疑忌。

translations.literal: Mingyue said: "Li Dingguo wavers toward Sun Kewang; one should ease pressure on Dingguo and use covert stratagem to make Kewang and Dingguo mutual suspects.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue wrote: "Li Dingguo has turned against Sun Kewang. Ease pressure on Dingguo and use stratagem to sow mutual suspicion between them.

sentences.zh: 我兵以守為戰，以屯為守，視隙而動。

translations.literal: Our troops should take defense as offense, garrison farming as defense, and strike when opportunity appears.
translations.idiomatic: Our armies should fight by holding ground, hold ground by farming garrison land, and strike when opportunity arises.

sentences.zh: 」上異之，擢工科給事中。

translations.literal: " The emperor was impressed and promoted him to supervising secretary of the Public Works section.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and appointed him supervising secretary of the Public Works section.

sentences.zh: 上經國遠圖疏，略言：「今國家所最急者，財也。

translations.literal: He submitted the memorial on far-reaching statecraft, stating in summary: "What the state most urgently needs now is revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial on long-term statecraft he wrote: "The state's most urgent need is revenue.
