sentences.zh: 歲入千八百一十四萬有奇，歲出二千二百六十一萬有奇。

translations.literal: Annual income is somewhat over 18.14 million; annual expenditure somewhat over 22.61 million.
translations.idiomatic: Annual revenue slightly exceeded 18.14 million taels; expenditure slightly exceeded 22.61 million.

sentences.zh: 出浮於入者四百四十七萬。

translations.literal: Expenditure exceeds income by 4.47 million.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditure exceeded income by 4.47 million taels.

sentences.zh: 國用所以不足，皆由養兵。

translations.literal: The reason state funds are insufficient is entirely maintaining troops.
translations.idiomatic: The shortfall owed entirely to maintaining armies.

sentences.zh: 各省鎮滿、漢官兵俸米、草豆，都計千八百三十八萬有奇，師行芻秣又百四十萬，其在京王公百官俸薪、披甲俸餉不過二百萬。

translations.literal: Manchu and Han garrison troops' salaries, grain, fodder, and beans in all provinces total somewhat over 18.38 million; campaign forage adds 1.4 million; princes, officials, and armored stipends in the capital are no more than 2 million.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Manchu and Han garrisons consumed over 18.38 million in salaries, grain, and fodder; campaign supplies another 1.4 million; capital stipends for princes, officials, and soldiers came to barely 2 million.

sentences.zh: 是則歲費二千二百萬，十分在養兵，一分在雜用也。

translations.literal: Thus annual expenditure of 22 million: ten parts for maintaining troops, one part for miscellaneous use.
translations.idiomatic: Of 22 million in annual spending, nine-tenths went to the army and one-tenth to everything else.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為今日不宜再議剝削以給兵餉，而當議就兵生餉之道。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks today one should not again discuss squeezing to supply military pay, but rather discuss how troops can generate their own pay.
translations.idiomatic: We should stop debating further cuts to fund the army and find a way for soldiers to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 河南、山東、湖廣、陝西、江南北、浙東西、江西、閩、廣諸行省，迭經兵火水旱，田多荒廢。

translations.literal: Henan, Shandong, Huguang, Shaanxi, Jiangnan north and south, Zhejiang east and west, Jiangxi, Fujian, Guangdong and other provinces, repeatedly afflicted by war, fire, and drought-flood, have much land abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Henan, Shandong, Huguang, Shaanxi, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, and Guangdong had seen repeated war, flood, and drought; much land lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 宜令各省駐防官兵分地耕種，稍仿明洪武中屯田之法，初年有司給與牛種、耕具、餼糧，自次年後，兵皆自食其力，便可不費朝廷金錢，此其為利甚溥。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order garrison troops in each province to divide land and farm, somewhat following Ming Hongwu garrison-farming methods; in the first year officials supply cattle, seed, farm tools, and rations; from the second year troops feed themselves—then the court need spend no money; the benefit is very broad.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison troops should be assigned land to farm, following Hongwu-era colony farming: officials supply cattle, seed, tools, and rations the first year; thereafter soldiers feed themselves at no cost to the treasury—a vast saving.

sentences.zh: 古者郡縣之兵，什伍相配，千百成旅，將帥因而轄之。

translations.literal: Anciently, prefecture and county troops were matched in squads of five and ten, hundreds and thousands forming companies; commanders thereby governed them.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity county troops were organized in fives and tens, hundreds and thousands, under their commanders.

sentences.zh: 乃者將帥多以僕從、摎役、優伶為兵，其實能操戈殺賊者十不得二三。

translations.literal: Nowadays commanders mostly use servants, attendants, and actors as soldiers; of those who can truly wield weapons and kill bandits, not two or three in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Today commanders fill ranks with servants, attendants, and actors—barely two or three in ten can actually fight.

sentences.zh: 故食糧有兵，充伍無兵。

translations.literal: Thus on the ration rolls there are soldiers; in the ranks there are none.
translations.idiomatic: The pay rolls are full, but the ranks are empty.

sentences.zh: 官去兵隨，難議屯種。

translations.literal: When officers leave, troops follow—difficult to discuss garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: Troops follow their officers when they transfer, making garrison farming impossible.

sentences.zh: 今當先定兵額，官有升降，兵無去來。

translations.literal: Now one should first fix troop quotas: officers may rise or fall, but soldiers neither leave nor come.
translations.idiomatic: Fix troop quotas first: officers may transfer, but soldiers stay put.

sentences.zh: 平定各省及去賊二三百里外者，皆給地課耕。

translations.literal: In pacified provinces and places two or three hundred li from bandits, all should be given land to farm on assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In pacified provinces and areas two or three hundred li from rebels, all soldiers should receive farmland.

sentences.zh: 因人之力與地之宜，一歲便可生財至千餘萬。

translations.literal: Through human labor and the land's suitability, in one year revenue can be generated to over ten million.
translations.idiomatic: With manpower and suitable land, a single year could yield over ten million taels.

sentences.zh: 群情不為深慮，不過議節省某項、清察某項。

translations.literal: Public sentiment gives no deep thought, discussing only saving on this item or auditing that item.
translations.idiomatic: Officials offer no deeper remedy—only debating minor savings here or audits there.

sentences.zh: 譬如盤水，何益旱田？

translations.literal: It is like lading water in a dish—what benefit to a drought-stricken field?
translations.idiomatic: That is like scooping water with a bowl to irrigate a drought—worthless.

sentences.zh: 臣見今日因賊而設兵，因兵而措餉，因餉而病民。

translations.literal: Your servant sees that today because of bandits troops are raised, because of troops pay is levied, because of pay the people are harmed.
translations.idiomatic: I see a vicious cycle: rebels require armies, armies require pay, pay harms the people.

sentences.zh: 民復為賊，展轉相因，深可隱憂。

translations.literal: The people again become bandits, turning in a cycle—deep cause for hidden worry.
translations.idiomatic: The people turn rebel in turn—a deeply alarming cycle.

sentences.zh: 要在力破因循，斷無不可核之兵，斷無不可耕之田，斷無不可生之財。

translations.literal: The key is to forcefully break inertia: assuredly there are no troops that cannot be audited, no land that cannot be farmed, no revenue that cannot be generated.
translations.idiomatic: We must break inertia: no troops that cannot be audited, no land that cannot be farmed, no revenue that cannot be earned.

sentences.zh: 」疏下各直省督撫，議格不行。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent to governors of all provinces; deliberation blocked it and it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to provincial governors but was blocked and never implemented.

sentences.zh: 世祖惡貪吏，令犯贓十兩以上籍沒。

translations.literal: Shizu hated corrupt officials and ordered that those guilty of bribes over ten taels have property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunzhi Emperor hated corrupt officials and ordered confiscation for bribes over ten taels.

sentences.zh: 命岳疏言：「立法愈嚴，而糾貪不止，病在舉劾不當。

translations.literal: Mingyue memorialized: "The more severe the law, the more corruption is pursued without end—the illness lies in improper impeachment and recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue wrote: "Harsher laws have not stopped corruption—the problem is improper impeachments.

sentences.zh: 請敕吏部，督撫按舉劾疏至，當參酌公論，果有賢者見毀，不肖者蒙譽，據實覆駁。

translations.literal: He requested that the Ministry of Personnel, when impeachment memorials from governors and censors arrive, weigh public opinion; where the worthy are slandered or the unworthy praised, rebut according to facts.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the Ministry of Personnel to weigh public opinion when provincial memorials arrive and rebut cases where the worthy are slandered or scoundrels praised.

sentences.zh: 如部臣耳目有限，科道臣皆得執奏。

translations.literal: If ministry officials' reach is limited, all supervising secretaries and censors may submit memorials.
translations.idiomatic: If ministry officials cannot see everywhere, all censorial officials should be allowed to memorialize.

sentences.zh: 又按臣原有都察院考核甄別，督撫本重臣，言官恐外轉為屬吏，參劾絕少。

translations.literal: Touring censors were originally evaluated and screened by the Censorate; governors are senior officials—censors fear that abroad they become subordinates, and impeachments are extremely few.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censors were once screened by the Censorate, but governors outrank them; fearing they become subordinates in the provinces, censors hardly ever impeach.

sentences.zh: 請特敕責成，簡別精實。

translations.literal: He requested special edicts assigning responsibility, selecting with precision and substance.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for special edicts holding them accountable with rigorous selection.

sentences.zh: 每歲終仍命吏部、都察院考核督撫舉劾當否，詳具以聞。

translations.literal: At year's end still order the Ministry of Personnel and Censorate to evaluate whether governors' impeachments were appropriate, reporting in detail.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end the Ministry of Personnel and Censorate should review whether governors' impeachments were sound and report.

sentences.zh: 庶激勵大法以倡率小廉。

translations.literal: Thus by enforcing the great law, small integrity may be led.
translations.idiomatic: Thus strict enforcement at the top would encourage modest integrity below.

sentences.zh: 」轉戶科。

translations.literal: " He transferred to the Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to the Revenue section.

sentences.zh: 再上疏論漕弊，大要謂：「百姓為運官所苦，運官又自有其苦，不得不苦百姓。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial on grain-transport abuses, saying in essence: "The people suffer at the hands of transport officials; transport officials also have their own suffering and cannot but make the people suffer.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on grain-transport abuses: "The people suffer from transport officials; transport officials suffer too, and pass that suffering to the people.

sentences.zh: 請革通倉需索，禁旗丁混搶，倉場督臣親監河兌。

translations.literal: He requested abolishing demands at transit granaries, prohibiting banner privates from indiscriminate looting, and having granary supervisors personally oversee river delivery.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed ending exactions at transit granaries, stopping banner privates from looting, and requiring granary supervisors to oversee river delivery personally.

sentences.zh: 」福建方用兵，時又苦旱，命岳疏陳五事，曰：緩徵買，糶勸賑，督催協餉，嚴治姦盜，安置投誠。

translations.literal: " Fujian was at war and also suffering drought; Mingyue memorialized five measures: easing purchase levies, selling grain to encourage relief, supervising and urging coordinated supplies, strictly punishing traitors and bandits, and settling those who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: With Fujian at war and in drought, Mingyue proposed five measures: ease requisition levies, sell grain for relief, coordinate military supplies, punish banditry, and settle defectors.

sentences.zh: 十五年，調兵科。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he transferred to the War section.
translations.idiomatic: In 1658 he transferred to the War section.

sentences.zh: 師下湖廣，命岳復申屯田之議，請復明軍衛屯田之制，設指揮、千百戶等官，以勞久功多之臣膺其任，子孫世及。

translations.literal: When the army went down to Huguang, Mingyue again pressed the garrison-farming proposal, requesting restoration of Ming military colony farming, establishing commanders and company officers, with long-serving meritorious ministers holding the posts, hereditary for their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: As armies advanced into Huguang, Mingyue again pressed garrison farming, proposing restored Ming colony units under commanders and company officers granted to long-serving meritorious men as hereditary posts.

sentences.zh: 無漕之地，專固封疆；

translations.literal: In places without grain transport, they should hold the frontier exclusively;
translations.idiomatic: Where there was no grain transport, they would defend frontiers;

sentences.zh: 有漕之地，即使領運。

translations.literal: In places with grain transport, they should at once take charge of transport.
translations.idiomatic: where there was, they would manage transport.

sentences.zh: 新附之將，有功亦得拜官。

translations.literal: Newly submitted generals, if meritorious, could also be appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: Newly surrendered generals with merit could also receive appointments.

sentences.zh: 量易其地，勿在本省。

translations.literal: Their lands should be assigned by measure and exchange, not within their home province.
translations.idiomatic: Their posts should be assigned outside their home provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言：「各省除荒之數，歲縮銀五百五十萬有奇。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "The figures for wasteland deductions in each province shrink annual revenue by somewhat over 5.5 million taels.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that wasteland tax exemptions cost over 5.5 million taels annually.

sentences.zh: 荒地以河南、山東為最多。

translations.literal: Wasteland is greatest in Henan and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Henan and Shandong had the most fallow land.

sentences.zh: 請選清正御史，督察二省田地，率諸州縣清丈，編造魚鱗圖冊。

translations.literal: He requested selecting upright censors to supervise the two provinces' fields, leading all prefectures and counties in clear survey, compiling fish-scale land registers.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed upright censors to supervise land surveys in both provinces and compile fish-scale registers.

sentences.zh: 他省除荒多者，如例均丈。

translations.literal: Other provinces with large wasteland deductions should likewise be uniformly surveyed.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces with large exemptions should be surveyed likewise.

sentences.zh: 」得旨舉行。

translations.literal: " Imperial approval was received and it was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and the policy was implemented.

sentences.zh: 命岳又上清丈事宜十餘條。

translations.literal: Mingyue again submitted over ten articles on survey procedures.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue submitted over ten detailed rules for the surveys.

sentences.zh: 明桂王既出邊，雲南猶未平。

translations.literal: After the Ming Prince of Gui had fled the border, Yunnan was still not pacified.
translations.idiomatic: After the Ming Prince of Gui fled, Yunnan remained unconquered.

sentences.zh: 命岳疏言：「雲南歲餉九百萬，而一省正雜賦稅都計十六萬有奇，是以九百萬營十六萬之地也。

translations.literal: Mingyue memorialized: "Yunnan's annual military pay is nine million, while the province's regular and miscellaneous taxes total somewhat over 160,000—thus nine million to garrison land worth 160,000.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue wrote: "Yunnan consumes nine million taels yearly while the province's entire tax revenue is barely 160,000—we spend nine million to hold land worth 160,000.

sentences.zh: 雲南原有舊屯萬一千一百七十一頃有奇，科糧三十八萬九千九百九十二石有奇。

translations.literal: Yunnan originally had old colony fields of somewhat over 11,171 qing, with grain tax of somewhat over 389,992 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan once had 11,171-plus qing of colony fields yielding 389,992-plus shi in grain tax.

sentences.zh: 請敕巡撫袁懋功責成原軍，換帖領種。

translations.literal: He requested edict to Governor Yuan Maogong to charge the original troops, exchange certificates and receive land to farm.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Governor Yuan Maogong to require original garrison troops to reclaim their land with new certificates.

sentences.zh: 暫發二十萬金，買牛辦種，借給軍民。

translations.literal: Temporarily allocate 200,000 taels to buy cattle and prepare seed, lending to troops and people.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred thousand taels should be issued temporarily for cattle and seed loans to soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 經年銷算，必無虧損，又可收復科糧舊額。

translations.literal: After a year of accounting, there will surely be no loss, and the old grain tax quota can also be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the accounts would balance without loss, restoring the old grain tax quota.

sentences.zh: 且官收額內，軍餘額外，每粟一石，價可三金，視今年每石十二金，已省餉費四分之三。

translations.literal: Moreover, within the official quota the army keeps the surplus beyond quota; each shi of grain can be valued at three taels, compared with twelve taels per shi this year—already saving three-fourths of supply costs.
translations.idiomatic: Within the official quota soldiers could keep surplus grain; at three taels per shi versus twelve this year, supply costs would drop by three-quarters.

sentences.zh: 庶幾兵食兼足，不至竭天下之物力以奉一隅。

translations.literal: Thus perhaps both military food and supplies may be sufficient, and not exhaust the empire's material resources to sustain one corner.
translations.idiomatic: Armies would be fed without exhausting the empire's resources for one remote corner.

sentences.zh: 」上可其奏，命發十萬金買牛辦種，修復舊屯。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his memorial and ordered one hundred thousand taels of gold issued to buy cattle, prepare seed grain, and restore the old military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial and ordered one hundred thousand taels disbursed to purchase oxen and seed grain and to restore the old garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 命岳乞假歸葬，還朝，疏言：「賊習於海戰，我師皆北人，不諳水性。

translations.literal: Mingyue requested leave to return home for a burial; returning to court, he submitted a memorial stating: 'The rebels are practiced in naval warfare; our troops are all northerners and do not understand water warfare.'
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue took leave to go home for a funeral. Back at court, he memorialized: "The rebels are skilled at sea fighting, while our forces are all northerners unaccustomed to the water."

sentences.zh: 惟有堵截隘港，禁絕接濟，嚴號令，輕徭賦，與民休息，使民不為賊，賊不得資。

translations.literal: One can only block narrow harbor passages, cut off all resupply, enforce strict orders, lighten corvée and taxes, and give the people rest — so that the people do not become rebels and the rebels gain no resources.
translations.idiomatic: The only course is to block the narrow harbors, sever all outside aid, enforce strict discipline, lighten taxes and corvée, and let the people recover — so that they do not turn rebel and the rebels receive no support.

sentences.zh: 久之必有系醜獻闕下者。

translations.literal: In time there will certainly be those who bind up the ringleaders and present them at court.
translations.idiomatic: In time, someone will surely bind up the ringleaders and deliver them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」吏部以浙江右布政員盡忠遷廣東左布政，命已下，命岳劾其貪穢，盡忠坐罷。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel had appointed Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Yuan Jinzhong of Zhejiang as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong; after the order was issued, Mingyue impeached him for corruption, and Jinzhong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel had already appointed Yuan Jinzhong, right provincial administration commissioner of Zhejiang, as left provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong when Mingyue impeached him for corruption; Jinzhong was dismissed as a result.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，使廣東還，遷刑科都給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kangxi reign he returned from a mission to Guangdong and was transferred to chief supervising censor of the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign, after returning from a mission to Guangdong, he was promoted to chief supervising censor of the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 時陳豹據南澳，尚為明守，命岳疏請招豹收南澳。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Bao held Nan'ao and still served Ming; Mingyue submitted a memorial requesting that Bao be recruited to recover Nan'ao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bao then held Nan'ao and still served the Ming cause; Mingyue memorialized asking that Bao be won over to recover the island.

sentences.zh: 尋以議獄未當，奪官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was stripped of office because of improper deliberation in a judicial case.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon stripped of his post for improper handling of a judicial case.

sentences.zh: 六年，畿輔旱，詔求直言。

translations.literal: In the sixth year there was drought in the capital region, and an edict sought forthright criticism.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year drought struck the capital region, and an edict called for candid remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 命岳家居，以天子方衝齡，宜覽古今，廣法戒，撰千秋寶鑑，書垂成，未進，卒。

translations.literal: Mingyue was at home; noting that the Son of Heaven was still in his minority, he held that he ought to review past and present, broaden moral warnings, and compile the Thousand-Year Precious Mirror. The book was nearly finished but never submitted before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue was living in retirement. Believing the emperor was still a minor, he set himself to review history, broaden moral lessons, and compile the Thousand-Year Precious Mirror. The work was nearly complete but never submitted when he died.

sentences.zh: =李森先=李森先，字琳枝，山東掖縣人。

translations.literal: =Li Senxian= Li Senxian, style Linzhi, a native of Ye County in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Senxian, whose style was Linzhi, came from Ye County in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the Chongzhen reign of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He was a jinshi of the Chongzhen era under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，自國子監博士考選江西道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he was selected through examination from Doctor of the Imperial Academy to supervising censor of the Jiangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he passed competitive selection from his post as doctor of the Imperial Academy to become supervising censor of the Jiangxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 啟睿親王發大學士馮銓貪穢及其子源淮諸不法狀，御史吳達，給事中許作梅、莊憲祖、杜立德，御史王守履、羅國士、鄧孕槐、桑芸等先後論劾。

translations.literal: He opened a memorial to Prince Regent Dorgon exposing the corruption of Grand Secretary Feng Quan and the illegal conduct of his son Yuanhuai; Supervising Censor Wu Da, Supervising Secretaries Xu Zuomei, Zhuang Xianzu, and Du Lide, and Supervising Censors Wang Shoulü, Luo Guoshi, Deng Yunhuai, Sang Yun, and others successively joined in impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized Prince Regent Dorgon exposing Grand Secretary Feng Quan's corruption and the illegal acts of his son Yuanhuai. Supervising Censor Wu Da, supervising secretaries Xu Zuomei, Zhuang Xianzu, and Du Lide, and supervising censors Wang Shoulü, Luo Guoshi, Deng Yunhuai, and Sang Yun followed with impeachments of their own.

sentences.zh: 睿親王於重華殿集大學士，刑部、科道諸臣，召銓等面質，以為無實跡，語詳銓傳，責森先啟請肆市語過當，奪官。

translations.literal: The Prince Regent assembled grand secretaries and officials of the Ministry of Punishments and the censorate at the Chonghua Hall, summoned Quan and others for face-to-face questioning, and found no substantiated facts — details are given in Quan's biography; Senxian was blamed for having opened the memorial with language requesting public execution that was excessive, and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Regent Dorgon convened grand secretaries and officials from the Ministry of Punishments and the censorate at Chonghua Hall, summoned Quan and the others for a hearing, and found no proof of wrongdoing — the full account is in Quan's biography. Senxian was censured for opening his memorial with an excessive call for public execution and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 世祖既親政，銓罷去。

translations.literal: After the Shizu Emperor took personal rule, Quan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shizu Emperor assumed personal rule, Quan was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 九年十一月，大學士範文程以劾銓諸疏進，上閱之竟，曰：「諸臣劾銓誠當，何為以此罷？

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year Grand Secretary Fan Wencheng submitted the memorials impeaching Quan; after reading them through, the Emperor said: 'The officials' impeachment of Quan was indeed justified — why were they dismissed for this?'
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the ninth year, Grand Secretary Fan Wencheng presented the memorials impeaching Quan. After reading them through, the emperor said, "The officials were right to impeach Quan — so why were they dismissed for it?"

sentences.zh: 」文程曰：「諸臣劾大臣，無非為君國，上當思所以愛惜之。

translations.literal: Wencheng said: "When officials impeach high ministers, it is always for the sake of ruler and state; Your Majesty should consider how to cherish them."
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng replied, "When censors impeach high ministers, they do so for the sake of ruler and realm. Your Majesty should think how to protect them."

sentences.zh: 且使大臣而能箝制言官，非細故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, if high ministers can muzzle censorial officials, that is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if ministers can silence the censors, that is no trifling matter.

sentences.zh: 」越數日，上諭吏部，諸臣以劾銓罷者皆起用，森先補原官。

translations.literal: A few days later the Emperor instructed the Ministry of Personnel that all officials dismissed for impeaching Quan should be reappointed; Senxian was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the emperor ordered the Ministry of Personnel to reinstate every official dismissed for impeaching Quan, and Senxian recovered his former post.

sentences.zh: 十三年，巡按江南，劾罷貪吏淮安推官李子燮、蘇州推官楊昌齡，論如律。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, while touring and inspecting Jiangnan, he impeached and dismissed the corrupt Huai'an magistrate Li Zixie and the Suzhou magistrate Yang Changling; they were sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, on an inspection tour of Jiangnan, he impeached and removed the corrupt magistrates Li Zixie of Huai'an and Yang Changling of Suzhou, who were sentenced as the law required.

sentences.zh: 巡蘇州，杖殺不法僧三遮、優王紫稼並為優張榜少年沈濬，一時震悚。

translations.literal: While inspecting Suzhou he had beaten to death the lawless monk Sanzhe, the actor Wang Zijia, and the young actor Shen Jun who had posted a placard for Wang — all at once the region was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: On his Suzhou tour he had the lawless monk Sanzhe, the actor Wang Zijia, and the young performer Shen Jun — who had posted a placard on Wang's behalf — beaten to death, sending shock through the region.

sentences.zh: 淮安吏張電臣坐侵蝕漕折銀一百二十兩有奇，例當追比，森先為疏請緩之。

translations.literal: The Huai'an clerk Zhang Dianchen was found guilty of embezzling more than one hundred twenty taels of grain-transport conversion silver; by regulation he should be pressed for repayment; Senxian submitted a memorial requesting leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai'an clerk Zhang Dianchen had embezzled a little over one hundred twenty taels of grain-transport conversion silver and, by rule, should have been pressed for repayment; Senxian memorialized asking that the case be eased.

sentences.zh: 上責森先徇縱，奪官，逮至京訊鞫，事白，復原官。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Senxian for partiality and leniency, stripped him of office, and had him brought to the capital for interrogation; when the facts were cleared he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused Senxian of favoritism, dismissed him, and had him brought to the capital for trial; once the facts were established, he was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 十五年，應詔陳言，略曰：「上孜孜圖治，求言詔屢下；

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, responding to an edict, he submitted a memorial in part stating: 'Your Majesty diligently seeks good government, and edicts soliciting criticism have been issued repeatedly;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, answering an imperial call, he memorialized in part: "Your Majesty labors tirelessly for good government, and edicts inviting criticism have gone out again and again;

sentences.zh: 而諸臣遲回觀望者，皆以從前言事諸臣，一經懲創，則流徙永錮，相率以言為戒耳。

translations.literal: yet officials who hesitate and hold back do so because those who spoke out before, once punished, were exiled and permanently barred — they have taken warning together against speaking.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials hang back because those who spoke before them, once punished, were exiled and permanently barred. They have learned as one to treat speech as dangerous.

sentences.zh: 臣以為欲開言路，宜先寬言官之罰。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that if the path of speech is to be opened, the penalties on censorial officials should first be lightened.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that to reopen the path of remonstrance, the punishments imposed on censors must first be eased.

sentences.zh: 如流徙諫臣李呈祥、季開生、魏琯、李裀、郝浴、張鳴駿等，皆與恩詔因公詿誤例相應。

translations.literal: Such exiled remonstrating officials as Li Chengxiang, Ji Kaisheng, Wei Guan, Li Yin, Hao Yu, and Zhang Mingjun all fall under the amnesty provision for those who erred in public duty.
translations.idiomatic: Exiled remonstrators such as Li Chengxiang, Ji Kaisheng, Wei Guan, Li Yin, Hao Yu, and Zhang Mingjun all qualify under the amnesty provision for officials who erred in the course of public duty.

sentences.zh: 倘蒙俯賜軫卹，使天下昭然知上寬宥直臣，在遠不遺。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would graciously show pity, the whole realm would clearly know that the throne pardons upright officials and does not abandon those far away.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would show them mercy, the realm would plainly see that the throne pardons upright ministers and does not forget those banished far away.

sentences.zh: 凡有言責者，有不洗心竭慮而興起者乎？

translations.literal: Would any who bear the duty of speech fail to purify their hearts, exhaust their efforts, and rise to speak?
translations.idiomatic: Then what censor would not set his heart to the task and speak out with all his strength?

sentences.zh: 」上責其市恩徇情，奪官，下刑部議，流徙尚陽堡，上​​仍寬之，復原官。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him for currying favor and partiality, stripped him of office, and referred the case to the Ministry of Punishments, which sentenced him to exile at Shangyang Fort; the Emperor still showed leniency and restored him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused him of currying favor and showing partiality, dismissed him, and sent the case to the Ministry of Punishments, which sentenced him to exile at Shangyang Fort; the emperor then relented and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 尋命察荒河南，用左都御史魏裔介言，給敕印，未訖事而卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to inspect famine in Henan; on the recommendation of Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie he was given imperial credentials and a seal, but died before the task was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to inspect famine relief in Henan and, on Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie's recommendation, received imperial credentials and a seal, but died before finishing the work.

sentences.zh: 十七年，上命吏部開列建言得罪諸臣，其流徙者，舉呈祥、琯、裀、開生及彭長庚、許爾安凡六人。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Emperor ordered the Ministry of Personnel to list officials punished for memorializing; among those exiled he named Chengxiang, Guan, Yin, Kaisheng, Peng Changgeng, and Xu Er'an — six men in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the emperor ordered the Ministry of Personnel to list officials punished for speaking out. Among the exiled he named Chengxiang, Guan, Yin, Kaisheng, Peng Changgeng, and Xu Er'an — six in all.

sentences.zh: 上命釋呈祥，許琯、開生歸葬。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Chengxiang released and permitted Guan and Kaisheng to return home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chengxiang freed and allowed Guan and Kaisheng to return home for burial.

sentences.zh: 餘雖係建言，情罪不同，無可寬免。

translations.literal: The rest, though also punished for memorializing, differed in circumstances and guilt and could not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The others, though also punished for remonstrance, differed in circumstances and offense and could not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 裀、開生自有傳。

translations.literal: Yin and Kaisheng have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin and Ji Kaisheng have biographies of their own elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 長庚、爾安事見睿親王傳。

translations.literal: The affairs of Changgeng and Er'an are recorded in the biography of the Prince Regent.
translations.idiomatic: The cases of Changgeng and Er'an are treated in the biography of Prince Regent Dorgon.

sentences.zh: 呈祥，字吉津，山東霑化人。

translations.literal: Chengxiang, style Jijin, a native of Zhanhua in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengxiang, style Jijin, came from Zhanhua in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the Chongzhen reign of Ming, selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Chongzhen era, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 順治初，授編修。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he was appointed Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷少詹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to junior tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，條陳部院衙門應裁去滿官，專用漢人。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year he submitted a detailed memorial that Manchu officials in ministry and court offices should be cut and Han Chinese alone employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the tenth year he memorialized that Manchu posts in the ministries and courts should be abolished and Han officials alone employed.

sentences.zh: 上諭大學士洪承疇等曰：「呈祥此奏甚不當。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Grand Secretaries Hong Chengchou and others: 'This memorial of Chengxiang's is very improper.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Grand Secretaries Hong Chengchou and the others, "Chengxiang's memorial is wholly out of line."

sentences.zh: 昔滿臣贊理庶政，弼成大業。

translations.literal: Formerly Manchu ministers assisted in governing the realm and helped accomplish the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Manchu ministers helped govern the realm and build this great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 彼時豈曾諮爾漢臣？

translations.literal: At that time were Han ministers ever consulted?
translations.idiomatic: Were Han ministers ever consulted in those days?

sentences.zh: 朕滿、漢一體眷遇，奈何反生異意耶？

translations.literal: I treat Manchu and Han as one body with equal favor — why should contrary intentions arise?
translations.idiomatic: I treat Manchu and Han as one and favor them equally — why should anyone now turn against that?

sentences.zh: 」副都御史宜巴漢等因劾呈祥，奪官，下刑部，坐呈祥巧言亂政，論斬，上命免死，流徙盛京。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yibahan and others thereupon impeached Chengxiang; he was stripped of office and sent to the Ministry of Punishments, which found him guilty of crafty speech disturbing government and sentenced him to decapitation; the Emperor ordered death commuted and exile to Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yibahan and others impeached Chengxiang. He was dismissed and sent to the Ministry of Punishments, which convicted him of using clever language to disturb government and sentenced him to death; the emperor commuted the sentence to exile in Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 居八年，至是命釋還，詣京師疏謝，遂還裡。

translations.literal: After eight years in exile he was now ordered released; he came to the capital to submit a memorial of thanks and then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years he was ordered released, came to the capital to offer thanks, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 琯，字昭華，山東壽光人。

translations.literal: Guan, style Zhaohua, a native of Shouguang in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan, style Zhaohua, came from Shouguang in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，官御史。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the Chongzhen reign of Ming; he served as supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Chongzhen era, he had served as supervising censor under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，以薦起原官，巡按甘肅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he was recommended and restored to his former post, touring and inspecting Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he was recommended back to his old post and sent on an inspection tour of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 請開馬市以柔遠人，下部議行。

translations.literal: He requested opening horse markets to conciliate distant peoples; the memorial was sent to the ministries for deliberation and put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that horse markets be opened to conciliate frontier peoples; the ministries approved and the policy was carried out.

sentences.zh: 涼州兵劫參議道廨，捕得倡亂者二十餘人，琯疏言西陲兵驕悍，由明季專事姑息，養奸滋亂，宜用重典。

translations.literal: Soldiers at Liangzhou raided the office of the participation-and-deliberation circuit; more than twenty ringleaders were captured. Guan memorialized that frontier troops were arrogant and fierce because the late Ming had indulged them exclusively, nourishing villains and breeding disorder — severe punishment should be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou soldiers raided the circuit intendant's yamen and more than twenty ringleaders were seized. Guan memorialized that frontier troops had grown arrogant because the late Ming had indulged them, breeding villains and disorder, and that severe punishment was needed.

sentences.zh: 上命悉誅之，並詔後有犯者，首從駢斬，著為令。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered all executed and also decreed that future offenders, leaders and followers alike, would be jointly beheaded — this was established as law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them all executed and decreed that future offenders, leaders and followers alike, would be beheaded together — a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 四年，授江寧學政。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed educational commissioner of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made educational commissioner of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 七年，還京，掌河南道。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he returned to the capital and took charge of the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he returned to the capital and took charge of the Henan censorial circuit.

sentences.zh: 八年，漕運總督吳惟華請輸銀萬，又括諸項羨餘，得九萬三千，請以助餉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Wu Weihua requested to remit ten thousand taels of silver and, by collecting various surpluses, obtained ninety-three thousand, which he asked to contribute toward military funds.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Wu Weihua offered ten thousand taels of silver and, by collecting assorted surpluses, raised ninety-three thousand more to assist military pay.

sentences.zh: 琯疏言淮、揚連年水旱，惟華輸餉皆分派屬吏，仍取自民間，乞賜察究，會巡漕御史張中元發惟華貪黷狀，逮治奪官。

translations.literal: Guan memorialized that Huai and Yang had suffered flood and drought year after year; Weihua's remittances were all apportioned to subordinate officials and still taken from the people — he begged investigation. At the same time Grain-Transport Touring Censor Zhang Zhongyuan exposed Weihua's corruption; he was arrested, tried, and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Guan memorialized that the Huai-Yang region had suffered repeated flood and drought, while Weihua's contributions were levied through subordinates and still drawn from the people; he asked for an inquiry. Touring censor of grain transport Zhang Zhongyuan then exposed Weihua's corruption, and Weihua was arrested and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 琯又劾鄖陽撫治趙兆麟，甄別文武屬吏，薦舉多至數十，糾劾僅一二微員，上為責兆麟，並誡諸督撫不得劾微員塞責。

translations.literal: Guan also impeached Yunyang pacification commissioner Zhao Zhaolin: in screening civil and military subordinates he recommended as many as several dozen while impeaching only one or two minor officials. The Emperor rebuked Zhaolin and admonished all governors-general and governors not to impeach minor officials merely to fulfill a quota.
translations.idiomatic: Guan also impeached Yunyang pacification commissioner Zhao Zhaolin for recommending dozens of subordinates while censuring only one or two minor officials. The emperor rebuked Zhao and warned all governors-general and governors not to satisfy quotas by targeting minor officials.

sentences.zh: 九年，授順天府府丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was promoted to president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 八旗逃人初屬兵部督捕，部議改歸大理寺，琯疏言其不便，乃設兵部督捕侍郎專董其事。

translations.literal: Eight Banner fugitives were at first pursued under the Ministry of War; when the ministry proposed transferring the duty to the Court of Judicial Review, Guan memorialized that this was inconvenient, and a vice minister of war was instead established specifically to supervise fugitive pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Banner fugitives had first been pursued under the Ministry of War. When the ministry proposed shifting the duty to the Court of Judicial Review, Guan argued against it, and a vice minister of war was instead appointed to supervise fugitive pursuit.

sentences.zh: 又言：「逃人日多，以投充者★。

translations.literal: He also stated: 'Fugitives grow daily in number because those who register as tou chong are numerous.'
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Fugitives increase by the day because those who register as tou chong are so numerous."

sentences.zh: 本主私縱成習，聽其他往，日久不還，概訟為逃人。

translations.literal: Masters have made a custom of privately releasing them and allowing them to go elsewhere; when they do not return for a long time, they are all sued as fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Masters routinely let them go elsewhere on private leave; when they failed to return, they were sued wholesale as fugitives.

sentences.zh: 逃人至再，罪止鞭百，而窩逃猶論斬，籍人口、財產給本主。

translations.literal: A fugitive caught a second time is punished by no more than one hundred lashes, yet harboring a fugitive is still punished by decapitation, with household members and property registered and given to the master.
translations.idiomatic: A repeat fugitive faced no more than one hundred lashes, yet harboring a fugitive still carried the death penalty, with the household and property confiscated and given to the master.

sentences.zh: 與叛逆無異，非法之平。

translations.literal: This is no different from treason and is not the evenhandedness of law.
translations.idiomatic: That is indistinguishable from punishing treason and is not equal justice under the law.

sentences.zh: 」下九卿議，改為流，免籍沒。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the Nine Ministers for deliberation; the penalty was changed to exile and confiscation of household registration was waived.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Ministers deliberated and changed the penalty to exile, waiving confiscation of household registration.

sentences.zh: 又言窩逃瘐斃，妻子應免流徙，時遇熱審，亦應一體減等。

translations.literal: He also stated that when a harborer of fugitives died in prison of illness, his wife and children should be exempt from exile; as the summer judicial review was then in session, they should likewise receive commutation as a body.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that when a harborer died in custody, his wife and children should be spared exile, and that during the summer judicial review such cases should be commuted as well.

sentences.zh: 上責其市恩，下王大臣議琯巧寬逃禁，當坐絞，上寬之，降授通政司參議。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him for courting favor; the case was sent to the princes and ministers, who held that Guan had craftily loosened the fugitive ban and deserved strangulation; the Emperor showed leniency and demoted him to participation secretary of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused him of currying favor. The princes and ministers found that Guan had craftily loosened the fugitive laws and deserved strangulation; the emperor relented and demoted him to participation secretary in the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 德州諸生呂煌窩逃事發，州官當坐罪，琯持異議。

translations.literal: When the case of the Licentiate Lü Huang harboring fugitives came to light in Dezhou, the prefectural officials should have been punished; Guan held a dissenting view.
translations.idiomatic: When the case of Dezhou licentiate Lü Huang harboring fugitives came to light, the prefectural officials were liable for punishment, but Guan dissented.

sentences.zh: 王大臣劾琯，因追議琯前請熱審減等為煌地，坐奪官，流徙遼陽，卒於戍所。

translations.literal: The princes and ministers impeached Guan and, revisiting his earlier request for commutation during the summer review as favoritism toward Huang, stripped him of office and exiled him to Liaoyang, where he died in banishment.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and ministers impeached Guan and, tracing his earlier plea for summer-review commutation to favoritism toward Huang, dismissed him and exiled him to Liaoyang, where he died in banishment.

sentences.zh: 上既許歸葬，並宥其孥還故里。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already permitted his body to be returned for burial and also pardoned his wife and children to return to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already allowed his body to be returned for burial and pardoned his wife and children to go home.

sentences.zh: 諸與森先同時劾馮銓者：吳達，江南人。

translations.literal: Among those who impeached Feng Quan at the same time as Senxian: Wu Da, a man of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who impeached Feng Quan alongside Senxian was Wu Da of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 自刑部員外郎授御史。

translations.literal: From vice director of the Ministry of Punishments he was appointed supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He had been promoted from vice director in the Ministry of Punishments to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 順治二年七月，疏言：「今日用人，皆取材於明季。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Shunzhi he submitted a memorial stating: 'Today's appointments all draw their material from the late Ming.'
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Shunzhi 2 he memorialized: "Today's appointments all draw on men from the late Ming."

sentences.zh: 抗直忤時，山林放棄，此明季所黜而今日當用者也。

translations.literal: Those upright and outspoken who offended their times and were abandoned in the hills — these the late Ming dismissed but today ought to be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Men who were upright, outspoken, and cast out in the hills — dismissed by the late Ming but the very men who should be used today.

sentences.zh: 逆黨權翼，貪墨敗類，此明季所黜而今日不可不黜者也。

translations.literal: Partisans of the usurping faction, corrupt and depraved men — these the late Ming dismissed and today cannot fail to dismiss.
translations.idiomatic: Partisans of the usurping faction and corrupt failures — dismissed by the late Ming and men who must be dismissed today as well.

sentences.zh: 持祿養交，倒行逆施，此明季未黜而今日不可不黜者也。

translations.literal: Those who clung to salary and cultivated connections, acting perversely — these the late Ming did not dismiss but today cannot fail to dismiss.
translations.idiomatic: Men who clung to salary, cultivated connections, and acted perversely — not dismissed by the late Ming, but men who must be dismissed today.

sentences.zh: 定鼎初年，藉招徠為名，猶可兼收邪正。

translations.literal: In the first years after the founding of the dynasty, under the name of recruitment, good and bad could still be gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: In the first years after the founding, recruitment could still bring in both the worthy and the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 江南既定，人材畢集，若复涇渭不分，則君子氣沮，宵小競進。

translations.literal: Now that Jiangnan is settled and talent is fully gathered, if pure and impure are again not distinguished, upright men will be discouraged and petty villains will rush forward.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiangnan pacified and talent fully gathered, if worthy and unworthy are not separated again, upright men will lose heart and petty men will rush forward.

sentences.zh: 即如阮大鋮、袁宏勳、徐復陽輩，聯袂而至，豈可概加錄用乎？

translations.literal: Take men such as Ruan Dacheng, Yuan Hongxun, and Xu Fuyang arriving in a body — can they all indiscriminately be appointed?
translations.idiomatic: Men like Ruan Dacheng, Yuan Hongxun, and Xu Fuyang came forward in groups — can they all be appointed without distinction?

sentences.zh: 至廣開言路，尤為創業急務。

translations.literal: As for broadly opening the path of speech, that is especially an urgent task in founding an enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Opening the path of remonstrance is especially urgent work for a founding dynasty.

sentences.zh: 乃動責回奏，是沮敢諫之氣而塞後進之路也。

translations.literal: Yet officials are constantly ordered to submit follow-up memorials — this dampens the spirit of bold remonstrance and blocks the way for those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: Yet censors are constantly ordered to submit follow-up memorials — that dampens bold remonstrance and blocks the way for those who follow.

sentences.zh: 即如趙開心論事爽剴，用其人矣，而所規切時政，果一一用之否耶？

translations.literal: Take Zhao Kaixin — his discussion of affairs is forthright and incisive, and the man has been employed; yet were his criticisms of current policy truly adopted one by one?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kaixin speaks forthrightly and has been employed — but were his criticisms of current policy truly acted on one by one?

sentences.zh: 」得旨：「朝廷用人，非曰誘之，若先既錄用，後無罪而黜，是有疑心矣。

translations.literal: He received an imperial response: "When the court employs men, it is not a matter of enticement; if one is first appointed and later dismissed without guilt, that would arouse suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: The response read: "When the court employs men, it is not to lure them in. If someone is appointed and later dismissed without guilt, that would breed suspicion."

sentences.zh: 屢飭回奏，欲求其實，非沮言路也。

translations.literal: Repeated orders for follow-up memorials seek substantiation of facts — this is not blocking the path of speech.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated orders for follow-up memorials seek facts, not a closing of the path of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 」疏寢不用。

translations.literal: The memorial was shelved and not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was set aside and not acted upon.

sentences.zh: 旋命巡按山東、湖南，官至太僕寺少卿。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to tour and inspect Shandong and Hunan; he rose to vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent on inspection tours of Shandong and Hunan and rose to vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 桑芸，山西榆次人。

translations.literal: Sang Yun, a native of Yuci in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Yun came from Yuci in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 自行人授御史，巡按順天，累遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: From courier he was appointed supervising censor, touring and inspecting Shuntian; he was promoted in succession to president of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: From courier he became supervising censor on an inspection tour of Shuntian and rose in succession to president of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 出為河南汝南道參政，督民墾荒土，除雜派，捕治巨猾斃杖下。

translations.literal: Sent out as administration commissioner of Runan Circuit in Henan, he supervised the people in reclaiming wasteland, abolished miscellaneous levies, and captured and punished great scoundrels, beating some to death.
translations.idiomatic: As administration commissioner of Runan Circuit in Henan, he supervised reclamation of wasteland, abolished miscellaneous levies, and captured major criminals, beating some to death under the rod.

sentences.zh: 累遷廣東左布政。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to left provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to left provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 道卒。

translations.literal: He died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He died en route.

sentences.zh: 又有許作梅，河南新鄉人。

translations.literal: There was also Xu Zuomei, a native of Xinxiang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Xu Zuomei of Xinxiang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 亦以劾銓罷，復起官至太僕寺少卿。

translations.literal: He too was dismissed for impeaching Quan; restored later, he rose to vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He too was dismissed for impeaching Quan, but was later restored and rose to vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 王守履，山西寧鄉人。

translations.literal: Wang Shoulü, a native of Ningxiang in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoulü came from Ningxiang in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 自工部郎中授御史，巡按湖北。

translations.literal: From director in the Ministry of Works he was appointed supervising censor, touring and inspecting Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: From director in the Ministry of Works he became supervising censor on an inspection tour of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 羅國士，山東德州人。

translations.literal: Luo Guoshi, a native of Dezhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Guoshi came from Dezhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 自禮部主事授御史，巡按順天。

translations.literal: From secretary in the Ministry of Rites he was appointed supervising censor, touring and inspecting Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: From secretary in the Ministry of Rites he became supervising censor on an inspection tour of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 莊憲祖，直隸東光人。

translations.literal: Zhuang Xianzu, a native of Dongguang, Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Xianzu came from Dongguang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 以明進士起戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He entered service as a supervising secretary of the Household Section upon his Ming-dynasty jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: Having earned his jinshi under the Ming, he began as a supervising secretary in the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 順治三年新進士，除科道，憲祖與吏科都給事中向玉軒疏爭，下刑部，並坐奪官。

translations.literal: When the new jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi were appointed to censorial posts, Xianzu and Xiang Yuxuan, chief supervising secretary of the Personnel Section, memorialized in protest; the matter was referred to the Ministry of Punishments and both were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3, when newly minted jinshi were posted to censorial offices, Xianzu and Chief Supervising Secretary Xiang Yuxuan of the Personnel Section protested in memorial; the case went to the Ministry of Punishments and both men lost their posts.

sentences.zh: 玉軒，四川通江人。

translations.literal: Yuxuan was a native of Tongjiang, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxuan came from Tongjiang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 鄧孕槐，失其籍，自順天府推官授御史，巡按江南。

translations.literal: Deng Yunhuai — his place of registration is lost to record — was appointed censor from his post as magistrate's assistant in Shuntian Prefecture and conducted an inspection tour of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yunhuai's native place is unrecorded; he rose from magistrate's assistant in Shuntian Prefecture to censor and toured Jiangnan as inspector.

sentences.zh: 李裀，字龍袞，山東高密人。

translations.literal: =Li Yin= Li Yin, style Longgun, native of Gaomi, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin, styled Longgun, was from Gaomi in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治六年，以舉人考授內院中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shunzhi, as a provincial degree-holder he was examined and appointed as a Hanlin Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 6 he passed an examination as a provincial graduate and was made a Hanlin Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 擢禮科給事中，轉兵科。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites Section and transferred to the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to supervising secretary in the Rites Section, he later moved to the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 劾吏部郎中宋學洙典試河南，宿妓納餽，鞫實，奪官。

translations.literal: He impeached Song Xuezhu, a bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, for staying with prostitutes and accepting gifts while presiding over examinations in Henan; the charges were substantiated and Song was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Song Xuezhu of the Ministry of Personnel for consorting with prostitutes and taking bribes while conducting exams in Henan; the case proved true and Song was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 八旗以俘獲為奴僕，​​主遇之虐，​​輒亡去。

translations.literal: The Eight Banners took captives as slaves and bond-servants; when masters treated them harshly, they would flee.
translations.idiomatic: Banner households kept war captives as bond-servants; when masters maltreated them, they fled.

sentences.zh: 漢民有原隸八旗為奴僕者，謂之「投充」，主遇之虐，​​亦亡去。

translations.literal: There were Han commoners who had originally been registered under the banners as bond-servants — called "registered dependents" (tou chong); when masters treated them harshly, they too fled.
translations.idiomatic: Han subjects once enrolled under the banners as bond-servants — known as "registered dependents" — likewise ran away when masters abused them.

sentences.zh: 逃人法自此起。

translations.literal: The fugitive law arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: This was how the fugitive-slave laws began.

sentences.zh: 十一年，王大臣議，匿逃人者給其主為奴，兩鄰流徙；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, princes and high ministers deliberated: those who concealed fugitives would be given to the original master as slaves, and the two neighbors would be banished;
translations.idiomatic: In year 11, princes and senior ministers ruled that harboring a fugitive made one a slave to the owner, with both neighbors banished;

sentences.zh: 捕得在途复逃，解子亦流徙。

translations.literal: if a captured fugitive escaped again en route, the escort officers would also be banished.
translations.idiomatic: and if a recaptured fugitive escaped again in transit, the escorting officers would be banished too.

sentences.zh: 上以其過嚴，命再議，仍如王大臣原議上。

translations.literal: The emperor deemed this excessively harsh and ordered reconsideration, but the original proposal of the princes and ministers was still submitted unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found this too severe and ordered another review, yet the princes' original proposal went forward unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十二年，裀上疏極論其弊曰：「皇上為中國主，其視天下皆為一家。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Yin submitted a memorial vigorously arguing the evils of the law, saying: "Your Majesty is sovereign of China and should regard all under Heaven as one household.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 Yin memorialized at length against the law: "You rule China and should see the empire as one household.

sentences.zh: 必別為之名曰'東人'，又曰'舊人'，已歧而二之矣。

translations.literal: Yet you insist on separate names — 'Easterners' and 'Old Ones' — splitting the people in two.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you distinguish 'Easterners' from 'Old Ones' — already dividing the realm in two.

sentences.zh: 謂滿洲役使軍伍，猶兵與民，不得不分；

translations.literal: It may be argued that Manchu military service and banner troops, like soldiers and civilians, must be kept apart;
translations.idiomatic: Banner military service may require a soldier–civilian divide;

sentences.zh: 州縣追攝逃亡，猶清勾逃兵，不得不嚴覈：是已。

translations.literal: and that prefectures and counties must hunt fugitives as strictly as mustered deserters — so far, so be it.
translations.idiomatic: and counties must pursue runaways as strictly as deserters — fair enough.

sentences.zh: 然立法過重，株連太多，使海內無貧富良賤，皆惴惴莫必旦夕之命。

translations.literal: Yet the law is too heavy and implicates too many, so that rich and poor, good and base alike tremble, never sure of surviving from one day to the next.
translations.idiomatic: But the penalties are crushing and the dragnet too wide: rich and poor alike live in dread, never knowing if they will see tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 人情洶懼，有傷元氣，可為痛心者一也。

translations.literal: People's hearts seethe with fear, damaging the vital energy of the realm — the first cause for grief.
translations.idiomatic: Fear spreads through the land and drains its vital strength — the first grief.

sentences.zh: 法立而犯者眾，當思其何利於隱匿而愍不畏死。

translations.literal: The law exists yet violations abound; one must ask what profit lies in concealment that makes men fearless of death.
translations.idiomatic: The law is on the books yet violations multiply — ask what profit makes men risk death to hide fugitives.

sentences.zh: 此必有居東人為奇貨，挾以為K1。

translations.literal: Surely there are those who hoard Easterners as scarce goods and use them as leverage.
translations.idiomatic: Surely some treat banner bond-servants as prized commodities and leverage them for profit.

sentences.zh: 殷實破家，奴婢為禍，名義蕩盡，可為痛心者二也。

translations.literal: Solid households are ruined, bond-servants become a calamity, and honor is swept away — the second cause for grief.
translations.idiomatic: Respectable families are ruined, servants become a scourge, and reputations are destroyed — the second grief.

sentences.zh: 犯法不貸，牽引不原，即大逆不道，無以加此。

translations.literal: No pardon for the offense, no mercy for those implicated — even treason could scarcely add more.
translations.idiomatic: No leniency for offenders, no relief for the implicated — not even treason could be harsher.

sentences.zh: 破一家即耗一家之貢賦，殺一人即傷一人之培養。

translations.literal: Ruin one household and you lose one household's tax tribute; kill one person and you destroy one person's nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Destroy a household and you lose its taxes; kill a person and you waste years of nurturing subjects.

sentences.zh: 十年生聚，十年教訓，今乃用逃人法戕賊之乎？

translations.literal: 'Ten years to gather the people, ten years to educate them' — will you now use the fugitive law to slaughter your own subjects?
translations.idiomatic: After years of gathering and teaching the people, will the fugitive law now be used to destroy them?

sentences.zh: 可為痛心者三也。

translations.literal: The third cause for grief.
translations.idiomatic: The third grief.

sentences.zh: 人情不甚相遠，使其居身得所，何苦相率而逃，況至三萬之多？

translations.literal: Human nature differs little: if they were well placed, why flee en masse — moreover to the number of thirty thousand?
translations.idiomatic: People do not differ so much: if treated properly, why would tens of thousands flee together?

sentences.zh: 其非盡懷鄉土、念親戚明矣。

translations.literal: Clearly they are not all yearning for home and kin.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly not all are simply homesick.

sentences.zh: 不思恩義維繫，但欲窮其所往，法愈峻，逃愈多，可為痛心者四也。

translations.literal: Instead of binding them with kindness and duty, you only hunt them to the ends of the earth; the harsher the law, the more who flee — the fourth cause for grief.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than bind them with kindness, you chase them everywhere; the stricter the law, the more who run — the fourth grief.

sentences.zh: 自逮捕起解，至提赴質審，道路驛騷，雞犬不寧。

translations.literal: From arrest through escort to trial, the roads and post stations are in uproar; neither hen nor dog knows peace.
translations.idiomatic: From arrest through escort to trial, roads and inns are in chaos; no household is left undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 無論其中冤陷實繁，而瓜蔓相尋，市鬻鋃鐺殆盡。

translations.literal: Setting aside the many wrongful accusations, the chain of implication goes on and on until market stalls sell out of manacles.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving aside countless false accusations, the web of implication spreads until manacles are sold out in the markets.

sentences.zh: 日復一日，生齒彫殘，誰復為皇上赤子？

translations.literal: Day after day the population withers — who will remain your Majesty's innocent children?
translations.idiomatic: Day by day the people waste away — who will remain as your loyal subjects?

sentences.zh: 可為痛心者五也。

translations.literal: The fifth cause for grief.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth grief.

sentences.zh: 又不特犯者為然，饑民流離，以譏察東人故，吏閉關，民扃戶，無所投止。

translations.literal: Nor is this limited to offenders: starving refugees wander, but because of scrutiny for Easterners, officials shut their gates and commoners bolt their doors, leaving nowhere to shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Nor is it only offenders: starving refugees roam, but officials and households alike shut their doors for fear of harboring banner fugitives, leaving nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 嗟此窮黎，朝廷方蠲租煮粥，衣而食之，奈何因逃人法迫而使斃？

translations.literal: Alas for these desperate poor — while the court remits taxes and serves porridge, clothing and feeding them, why drive them to death through the fugitive law?
translations.idiomatic: Even as the court remits taxes and feeds the poor, the fugitive law drives them to die.

sentences.zh: 可為痛心者六也。

translations.literal: The sixth cause for grief.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth grief.

sentences.zh: 婦女躅躑於郊原，老稚僵僕於溝壑。

translations.literal: Women stumble across the open country; old and young lie stiff in ditches and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Women wander the countryside; old and young freeze in ditches.

sentences.zh: 強有力者，犯霜露，冒雨雪，東西迫逐，勢必鋌而走險。

translations.literal: The strong, braving frost and snow in pursuit east and west, will inevitably take desperate paths.
translations.idiomatic: The desperate, hunted through frost and snow, will surely turn to violence.

sentences.zh: 今寇孽未靖，招撫不遑，本我赤子，乃驅之作賊乎？

translations.literal: Rebels are not yet pacified and there is no time for reconciliation — will you drive your own subjects to become bandits?
translations.idiomatic: With rebels still abroad and pacification unfinished, will you turn your own people into bandits?

sentences.zh: 可為痛心者七也。

translations.literal: The seventh cause for grief.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh grief.

sentences.zh: 臣謂與其嚴於既逃之後，何如嚴於未逃之先？

translations.literal: Your servant says: rather than being harsh after they flee, would it not be better to be strict before they flee?
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to prevent flight than punish it after the fact.

sentences.zh: 今逃人三次始行正法，其初犯再犯，不過鞭責。

translations.literal: Today execution comes only on the third escape; first and second offenses draw only whipping.
translations.idiomatic: Now execution waits until a third escape; first and second offenses earn only lashes.

sentences.zh: 請敕今後逃人初犯即論死，皇上好生如天，不忍殺之，當仿竊盜刺字之例：初逃再逃，皆於面臂刺字。

translations.literal: I request that hereafter even a first offense be capital; if Your Majesty, merciful as Heaven, will not kill them, let it follow the tattooing of thieves: first and second flights should be marked on face and arm.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that first-time fugitives face death; if mercy forbids killing, tattoo face and arm on first and second flight, as with thieves.

sentences.zh: 則逃人不敢逃，即逃人自不敢留矣。

translations.literal: Then fugitives would not dare flee, and none would dare harbor them.
translations.idiomatic: Then none would flee — or shelter fugitives.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，留中。

translations.literal: " The memorial entered but was held without action.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received but filed without reply.

sentences.zh: 後十餘日，下王大臣會議，僉謂所奏雖於律無罪，然「七可痛」，情由可惡，當論死，上弗許，改議杖，徙寧古塔；

translations.literal: More than ten days later it went to joint deliberation by princes and ministers, all saying that although the memorial was not criminal in law, the "seven griefs" showed malicious intent and deserved death; the emperor refused and substituted beating and exile to Ningguta;
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later princes and ministers met: though not technically criminal, the "seven griefs" showed malign intent and merited death; the emperor refused and ordered beating and exile to Ningguta instead;

sentences.zh: 上命免杖，安置尚陽堡。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered the beating remitted and Yin sent to Shangyangbao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remitted the beating and sent him to Shangyang Fortress.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒。

translations.literal: After a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died.

sentences.zh: 上深知逃人法過苛重，絀王大臣議罪裀。

translations.literal: The emperor well knew the fugitive law was excessively harsh and rebuked the princes and ministers for their sentencing of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing the fugitive law was too harsh, the emperor rebuked the princes for their judgment on Yin.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月，諭曰：「朕念滿洲官民人等，攻戰勤勞，佐成大業。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year, an edict said: "We reflect that Manchu officials and people toiled in battle and helped establish the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 13 the emperor said: "I remember how Manchu officials and people fought tirelessly to build this dynasty.

sentences.zh: 其家役使之人，皆獲自艱辛，加之撫養。

translations.literal: The servants in their households were all obtained through hardship and are raised and cared for.
translations.idiomatic: The servants in their households were won through hardship and raised with care.

sentences.zh: 乃十餘年間，背逃日眾，隱匿尤多，特立嚴法。

translations.literal: Yet over more than ten years desertions daily increased and concealment grew, so We established strict laws.
translations.idiomatic: Yet over a decade desertions mounted and concealment spread, forcing strict laws.

sentences.zh: 以一人之逃匿而株連數家，以無知之奴僕而累及官吏，皆念爾等數十年之勞苦，萬不得已而設，非朕本懷也。

translations.literal: Implicating several households for one person's flight, and involving officials because of unknowing bond-servants — all this was set up, most reluctantly, thinking of your decades of toil; it is not Our original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing whole households for one fugitive and dragging officials into bond-servants' crimes was meant, reluctantly, to honor your decades of service — not my wish.

sentences.zh: 爾等當思家人何以輕去，必非無因。

translations.literal: You should consider why your household members leave so lightly — surely there is cause.
translations.idiomatic: Ask yourselves why servants flee — there must be reasons.

sentences.zh: 爾能容彼身，彼自體爾心。

translations.literal: If you can accommodate their persons, they will respond to your hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Treat them well and they will respond in kind.

sentences.zh: 若專恃嚴法，全不體恤，逃者仍眾，何益之有？

translations.literal: If you rely only on harsh law without sympathy, fugitives will still be many — what benefit is there?
translations.idiomatic: Rely only on harsh laws without kindness and fugitives will still abound — what good does that do?

sentences.zh: 朕為萬國主，犯法諸人，孰非天生烝民，朝廷赤子？

translations.literal: We are sovereign of all nations; of those who violate the law, who is not Heaven-born people, the court's own children?
translations.idiomatic: As sovereign of all nations, are lawbreakers not all Heaven's people and the court's own children?

sentences.zh: 今後宜體朕意省改，使奴僕充盈，安享富貴。

translations.literal: Henceforth you should heed Our intent, reform yourselves, keep your servants full in number, and enjoy wealth and honor in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter heed my intent: reform your ways, keep full households, and enjoy your prosperity in peace.

sentences.zh: 」十五年五月，复諭曰：「督捕逃人事例，屢令會議，量情申法，衷諸平允。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the fifteenth year, another edict said: "Regulations for pursuing fugitives have been repeatedly deliberated; the law should be applied according to circumstances with balanced justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 15 another edict said: "Fugitive regulations have been debated repeatedly; apply the law with balanced justice according to circumstances.

sentences.zh: 年來逃人未止，小民牽連，被害者多。

translations.literal: In recent years fugitives have not ceased and common people have been implicated; many have suffered harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fugitives persist and common people suffer in the dragnet.

sentences.zh: 聞有奸徒假冒逃人，詐害百姓，將殷實之家指為窩主，挾詐不已，告到督捕，冒主認領，指詭作真。

translations.literal: We hear that villains impersonate fugitives to extort the people, denouncing solid households as harborers, endlessly threatening; when reported to the pursuit office, they falsely claim ownership and turn deception into truth.
translations.idiomatic: Rogues impersonate fugitives to extort solid households as harborers; at the pursuit office they falsely claim ownership and turn lies into fact.

sentences.zh: 種種詐偽，重為民害。

translations.literal: Such frauds multiply and again harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: Such frauds plague the people afresh.

sentences.zh: 如有旗下姦宄橫行，許督撫逮捕，並本主治罪。

translations.literal: If banner rogues commit outrages, governors are permitted to arrest them and punish the owners as well.
translations.idiomatic: If banner ruffians run rampant, governors may arrest them and punish their masters too.

sentences.zh: 」逃人禍自此漸熄。

translations.literal: " From this the calamity of fugitives gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: After this the fugitive crisis slowly abated.

sentences.zh: =季開生=季開生，字天中，江南泰興人。

translations.literal: =Ji Kaisheng= Ji Kaisheng, style Tianzhong, native of Taixing, Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kaisheng, styled Tianzhong, came from Taixing in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the sixth year of Shunzhi, appointed Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 6 jinshi, he was made a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He rose through promotion to supervising secretary of the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supervising secretary in the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 明將張名振犯上海，開生疏言防禦海寇，宜遠偵探，扼要害，備器械，嚴海禁，杜接濟，密譏察。

translations.literal: When Ming general Zhang Mingzhen raided Shanghai, Kaisheng memorialized on coastal defense: distant reconnaissance, holding key points, stockpiling arms, strict sea bans, cutting off resupply, and secret surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming general Zhang Mingzhen attacked Shanghai, Kaisheng urged coastal defense through distant scouting, holding choke points, arming defenses, tightening sea bans, blocking resupply, and secret surveillance.

sentences.zh: 十一年，因地震，疏言：「地道不靜，民不安也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on account of an earthquake, he memorialized: "The earth is unsettled because the people are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11, after an earthquake, he wrote: "When the earth trembles, the people are unsettled.

sentences.zh: 民之不安，官失職也。

translations.literal: When the people are unsettled, officials have failed in duty.
translations.idiomatic: When people are unsettled, officials have failed.

sentences.zh: 官之失職，約有十端：一曰格詔旨，二曰輕民命，三曰縱屬官，四曰庇胥吏，五曰重耗剋，六曰納餽遺，七曰廣株連，八曰閣詞訟，九曰失彈壓，十曰玩糾劾。

translations.literal: When officials fail in duty, there are roughly ten causes: first, disregarding imperial edicts; second, treating people's lives lightly; third, indulging subordinate officials; fourth, shielding clerks; fifth, heavy exactions; sixth, accepting gifts; seventh, broad implication; eighth, blocking lawsuits; ninth, failing to suppress unrest; tenth, treating impeachment lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Official failure has ten causes: disregarding edicts, treating lives lightly, indulging subordinates, shielding clerks, heavy exactions, taking bribes, broad implication, blocking lawsuits, failing to suppress unrest, and treating impeachment lightly.

sentences.zh: 」分疏其目以上，章下所司。

translations.literal: " He submitted separate memorials detailing each item to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: He filed separate memorials on each point to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 調兵科右給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right supervising secretary of the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to right supervising secretary of the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 十二年秋，乾清宮成，發帑遣內監往江南採購陳設器皿，民間訛言往揚州買女子，開生上疏極諫。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twelfth year, when the Hall of Heavenly Purity was completed, the treasury dispatched eunuchs to Jiangnan to purchase furnishings and vessels; rumor spread that they were going to Yangzhou to buy girls, and Kaisheng memorialized in strong protest.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year 12, after the Hall of Heavenly Purity was finished, eunuchs were sent to Jiangnan to buy furnishings; rumors said they would buy girls in Yangzhou, and Kaisheng protested sharply.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「太祖、太宗制度，宮中從無漢女。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "The institutions of Taizu and Taizong never included Han women in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The reply said: "Taizu and Taizong never kept Han women in the palace.

sentences.zh: 朕奉皇太后慈訓，豈敢妄行，即太平後尚且不為，何況今日？

translations.literal: We follow the Empress Dowager's kindly instruction — how would We act rashly? Even in times of peace We would not do so — how much less today?
translations.idiomatic: I follow the Empress Dowager's instruction — how could I act rashly? Even in peace I would not — how much less now?

sentences.zh: 朕雖不德，每思效法賢聖主，朝夕焦勞。

translations.literal: Though We lack virtue, We daily strive to emulate sage rulers, toiling from dawn to dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Though I lack virtue, I daily strive to emulate sage rulers, toiling from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 若買女子入宮，成何如主耶？

translations.literal: If We bought girls for the palace, what sort of ruler would that make?
translations.idiomatic: If I bought girls for the palace, what sort of ruler would I be?

sentences.zh: 」因責開生肆誣沽直，下刑部杖贖，流尚陽堡，尋卒戍所。

translations.literal: " Kaisheng was therefore rebuked for slanderous remonstrance to win reputation; the Ministry of Punishments ordered beating commutable by ransom and exile to Shangyangbao; he soon died in banishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was rebuked for slanderous remonstrance to win reputation, beaten and ransomed, and exiled to Shangyang Fortress, where he soon died.

sentences.zh: 十七年，旱，下詔罪己，命吏部察謫降言官，諭曰：「季開生建言，原從朕躬起見，準复官歸葬，廕一子入監讀書。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, amid drought, an edict of self-reproach was issued; the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to review demoted remonstrating officials; an edict said: "Ji Kaisheng's remonstrance arose from concern for Our person; permit restoration of rank, burial at home, and enrollment of one son in the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17, during drought, the emperor issued a penitential edict and ordered review of demoted censors: "Ji Kaisheng spoke from concern for my person; restore his rank, allow burial at home, and enroll one son in the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 弟振宜，字詵兮。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zheny, style Shenxi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zheny, styled Shenxi.

sentences.zh: 順治四年進士，授浙江蘭溪知縣。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the fourth year of Shunzhi, appointed magistrate of Lanxi, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 4 jinshi, he was made magistrate of Lanxi in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 行取刑部主事，遷戶部員外郎、郎中。

translations.literal: Selected for the capital as a bureau secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, then promoted to vice bureau director and bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited to the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, he rose to vice director and director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十五年，考選浙江道御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, selected by examination as censor of the Zhejiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he passed an examination and became censor of the Zhejiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 及上以旱下詔罪己，言十二、十三年間，時有過舉。

translations.literal: When the emperor issued a drought edict of self-reproach, mentioning missteps in the twelfth and thirteenth years,
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's drought edict of self-reproach mentioned missteps in years 12 and 13,

sentences.zh: 振宜疏言：「伏讀上諭，興革責之部院，條奏責之科道，而內閣諸臣闕焉未及。

translations.literal: Zheny memorialized: "Having read Your Majesty's edict, reform is charged to the ministries and boards, detailed proposals to the censorate — yet the Grand Secretariat is passed over.
