translations.idiomatic: Zheny wrote: "Your edict charges ministries with reform and censors with proposals — yet says nothing of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 夫用人行政，其將用未用、將行未行之際，毫釐千里，間不容髮。

translations.literal: In appointing men and executing policy, at the moment between intention and action, the slightest deviation spans a thousand li — there is no room for delay.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing men and executing policy, the gap between intent and action admits no delay.

sentences.zh: 天顏咫尺，呼吸可通者，惟內閣諸臣。

translations.literal: Those who can reach the imperial countenance at arm's length are the Grand Secretaries alone.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Grand Secretaries stand within a breath of the throne.

sentences.zh: 皇上親政以來，憂勤惕厲，原未見有過舉。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty took personal rule, diligent and vigilant, there has truly been no misstep.
translations.idiomatic: Since you took personal rule, diligent and vigilant, there has truly been no misstep.

sentences.zh: 皇上以為有過舉矣，試問其時有言及者乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty believes there were missteps — were there any who spoke of them at the time?
translations.idiomatic: You believe there were missteps — did anyone speak of them at the time?

sentences.zh: 則宰相之不言亦可見矣。

translations.literal: Then the chief minister's silence is plain to see.
translations.idiomatic: Then the chief minister's silence speaks for itself.

sentences.zh: 皇上以心膂股肱寄之內閣諸臣，徒以票擬四五字了宰相事業，皇上縱不譴責，清夜捫心，恐有難以自慰者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty entrusts the Grand Secretaries as heart, spine, and thigh — yet they dismiss the work of chief minister with four or five characters of draft approval; even if Your Majesty does not rebuke them, in quiet nights they must find it hard to face themselves.
translations.idiomatic: You entrust the Grand Secretaries as your closest ministers — yet they reduce the chief minister's work to a few characters of draft approval; even without rebuke, can they face themselves at night?

sentences.zh: 」得旨：「閣臣不能盡言，初非其罪。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "That the Grand Secretaries do not speak fully is not originally their fault.
translations.idiomatic: The reply said: "That the Grand Secretaries do not speak fully is not originally their fault.

sentences.zh: 前諭十二、十三年間過舉，皆已行之事。

translations.literal: The earlier mention of missteps in the twelfth and thirteenth years referred to matters already done.
translations.idiomatic: The missteps in years 12 and 13 referred to matters already done.

sentences.zh: 朕心過失，即今豈能盡無，閣臣何由得知？

translations.literal: Errors in Our heart — how can they be wholly absent even now? How could the Grand Secretaries know?
translations.idiomatic: Errors in my heart — how can they be wholly absent even now? How could the Grand Secretaries know?

sentences.zh: 部覆章奏，照擬票發，皆朕親裁，亦非閣臣之咎。

translations.literal: When ministries reply to memorials and draft recommendations for issuance, all is personally decided by Us — this too is not the Grand Secretaries' fault.
translations.idiomatic: When ministries reply to memorials and draft recommendations for issuance, I decide personally — this too is not the Grand Secretaries' fault.

sentences.zh: 朕恆慮此心稍懈，諸臣其各加內省！

translations.literal: We constantly fear this heart may slacken — let every minister look inward!
translations.idiomatic: I constantly fear my resolve may slacken — let every minister look inward!

sentences.zh: 左都御史魏裔介疏劾大學士劉正宗蠹國亂政，振宜亦疏舉正宗樹黨納賄諸罪狀，正宗以是得罪。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie memorialized impeaching Grand Secretary Liu Zhengzong for corrupting the state and disordering government; Zhenyi also memorialized listing Zhengzong's crimes of forming factions and accepting bribes, and Zhengzong was punished on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie memorialized against Grand Secretary Liu Zhengzong for corrupting the state and ruining governance, and Zhenyi also submitted a memorial detailing Zhengzong's faction-building and bribery. On these charges Zhengzong fell.

sentences.zh: 互見正宗傳。

translations.literal: See also the biography of Zhengzong.
translations.idiomatic: See also the biography of Liu Zhengzong.

sentences.zh: 振宜又疏言：「府庫已竭，兵革方興。

translations.literal: Zhenyi again memorialized, saying: "The treasury is exhausted and warfare is just arising.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyi memorialized again: "The treasury is empty and war is breaking out.

sentences.zh: 雲南守禦，專任平西王，滿兵抽十之四五駐湖南。

translations.literal: For the defense of Yunnan, entrust it entirely to the Prince of Pingxi; withdraw four or five tenths of the Manchu troops to garrison Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's defense should be left entirely to the Prince of Pingxi, with four or five tenths of the Manchu garrison withdrawn to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功為閩、浙、江南三省之患，當擇地駐兵，絕其登陸。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong is a scourge to the three provinces of Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangnan; troops should be stationed at chosen points to cut off his landings.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong threatens Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangnan alike; troops should be posted at strategic points to block his landings.

sentences.zh: 閩撫徐永楨、浙督趙國祚、浙撫史記功，軍旅皆不嫺習，宜簡賢員以代其任。

translations.literal: Fujian Governor Xu Yongzhen, Zhejiang Governor-General Zhao Guozuo, and Zhejiang Governor Shi Jigong are all unskilled in military affairs; worthy men should be selected to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian Governor Xu Yongzhen, Zhejiang Governor-General Zhao Guozuo, and Zhejiang Governor Shi Jigong are none of them versed in military affairs; able men should be chosen to replace them.

sentences.zh: 山東、河南輔翼京師，連年水旱，盜賊實繁。

translations.literal: Shandong and Henan flank the capital; year after year of flood and drought have made bandits truly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong and Henan shield the capital, yet floods and droughts have piled up year after year, and bandits are truly rampant.

sentences.zh: 北直八府，白晝公行劫掠。

translations.literal: In the eight prefectures of Zhili, robbery is openly carried out in broad daylight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eight prefectures of Zhili, robbers now plunder openly in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 明末流寇，殷鑑不遠。

translations.literal: The roving bandits at the end of the Ming are a recent warning not far off.
translations.idiomatic: The roving rebels of the late Ming are a warning still fresh in memory.

sentences.zh: 蒙古闌入陝西洮、岷一帶耕種，西寧抵宣、大，長城頹塌，防衛空虛。

translations.literal: Mongols intrude to farm in the Tao and Min region of Shaanxi; from Xining to Xuanfu and Datong the Great Wall is crumbling and defenses are hollow.
translations.idiomatic: Mongols cross in to farm the Tao and Min districts of Shaanxi; from Xining to Xuanfu and Datong the Great Wall lies in ruins and the defenses are empty.

sentences.zh: 國家中外一統，疆界原宜分明，何可聽其出入不加譏察？

translations.literal: The state is unified within and without; boundaries ought by rights to be clear—how can their coming and going be allowed without inspection?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is one within and without; its borders ought to be clearly defined. How can their crossings be tolerated without scrutiny?

sentences.zh: 」又請復六科封駁舊制，復以揚、徐近河諸縣加派河夫為民間重累，疏請申禁，下部議行。

translations.literal: " He also requested restoration of the old system whereby the Six Sections could seal and return memorials, and again noted that the extra assignment of river corvée labor to counties near rivers in Yangzhou and Xuzhou was a heavy burden on the people; he memorialized requesting strict prohibition, and the matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked that the old practice of the Six Sections sealing and returning memorials be restored, and argued that the added river-corvée levies on counties near the waterways in Yangzhou and Xuzhou were crushing the people; his memorial was referred to the ministries for action.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡視河東鹽政。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to inspect salt administration east of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to inspect salt administration east of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 乞歸，卒。

translations.literal: He requested leave to retire and died.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire and died.

sentences.zh: 順治初以建言名者，又有給事中常若柱、張國憲。

translations.literal: Among those famed in the early Shunzhi reign for memorializing were also Supervising Secretaries Chang Ruozhu and Zhang Guoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Others who won fame in the early Shunzhi reign for speaking out were Supervising Secretaries Chang Ruozhu and Zhang Guoxian.

sentences.zh: 若柱疏言：「賊相牛金星弒君殘民，抗拒王師，力盡始降，宜嬰顯戮。

translations.literal: Ruozhu memorialized, saying: "The rebel chancellor Niu Jinxing murdered his sovereign and ravaged the people, resisted the royal army, and only surrendered when his strength was spent—he ought to suffer public execution.
translations.idiomatic: Ruozhu wrote: "The rebel chancellor Niu Jinxing murdered his lord, brutalized the people, and resisted the imperial armies until his strength was spent; he deserves public execution.

sentences.zh: 乃復玷列卿寺，靦顏朝右。

translations.literal: Yet he again disgraces the ranks of the Nine Ministers, shamelessly standing at the right of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he again holds a post among the Nine Ministers, brazenly taking his place at court.

sentences.zh: 其子銓同父作賊，冒濫為官，任湖廣糧儲道，贓私鉅萬。

translations.literal: His son Quan, like his father a bandit, obtained office by improper means, served as Grain Intendant of Huguang, and amassed bribes in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan followed his father into rebellion, then bought his way into office as Grain Intendant of Huguang, amassing bribes in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 請將金星父子立正國法，以申公義，快人心。

translations.literal: I request that father and son Jinxing be punished according to the law of the state, to uphold public justice and satisfy the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that father and son be punished under the law of the land, to uphold justice and satisfy the people.

sentences.zh: 」得旨：「流賊偽官投誠者，多能效力。

translations.literal: " An edict responded: "Among the false officials of the roving bandits who surrendered, many have been able to serve effectively.
translations.idiomatic: " The response came: "Many of the surrendered rebel officials have proved useful.

sentences.zh: 若柱此奏，殊不合理，應議處。

translations.literal: Ruozhu's present memorial is quite unreasonable and he should be subject to disciplinary action.
translations.idiomatic: Ruozhu's memorial is wholly unreasonable and merits disciplinary action.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷歸。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: " He was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 國憲疏言：「前朝廠衛之弊，如虎如狼，如鬼如蜮。

translations.literal: Guoxian memorialized, saying: "The abuses of the factory guards in the previous dynasty were like tigers and wolves, like ghosts and demons.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxian wrote: "The factory guards of the previous dynasty were as fierce as tigers and wolves, as sinister as ghosts and demons.

sentences.zh: 今易錦衣為鑾儀，此輩無能，逞其故智。

translations.literal: Today the Embroidered Uniform Guard has been replaced by the Imperial Procession Guard; these men lack ability and cannot display their old tricks.
translations.idiomatic: The Embroidered Uniform Guard has been replaced by the Imperial Procession Guard, and those men no longer have the power to play their old tricks.

sentences.zh: 乃臣聞有緝事員役在內院門首，訪察賜畫。

translations.literal: Yet your servant has heard that investigative agents are at the gate of the Inner Court, spying on the bestowal of imperial portraits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have heard that investigative agents stand at the Inner Court gate, watching who receives the imperial portrait.

sentences.zh: 賜畫特典，內院重地，安所用其訪察？

translations.literal: The bestowal of portraits is a special grace; the Inner Court is a weighty place—what need is there for such investigation?
translations.idiomatic: The imperial portrait is a special honor, and the Inner Court is sacred ground—why should anyone be investigating there?

sentences.zh: 城狐社鼠，小試其端。

translations.literal: Like foxes under the city wall and rats in the temple, they are testing the first edge of their power.
translations.idiomatic: Like foxes under the wall and rats in the shrine, they are testing how far they can go.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂宜大為之防也。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that great precautions ought to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: I believe strong precautions are needed now.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下廷臣議禁止，得旨：「鑾儀衛專司扈從，訪役緝事，一概禁止。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, court officials were ordered to deliberate on prohibition, and an edict responded: "The Imperial Procession Guard is devoted solely to escort duty; investigative and surveillance agents are altogether forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to court for deliberation, and the response came: "The Imperial Procession Guard exists only for escort duty; all investigative surveillance is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 」廠衛之禍始息。

translations.literal: " The calamity of the factory guards then began to subside.
translations.idiomatic: " Only then did the scourge of the factory guards begin to fade.

sentences.zh: 若柱，陝西蒲城人。

translations.literal: Ruozhu was a native of Pucheng, Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ruozhu came from Pucheng in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治四年進士，自庶吉士改戶科給事中。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Shunzhi, he was transferred from Hanlin Bachelor to Supervising Secretary of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi 4, he moved from Hanlin Bachelor to Supervising Secretary of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 國憲，順天宛平人。

translations.literal: Guoxian was a native of Wanping, Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxian came from Wanping in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，除吏科給事中。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi 3, he was appointed Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: =張煊=張煊，山西介休人。

translations.literal: =Zhang Xuan= Zhang Xuan, native of Jiexiu, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan, from Jiexiu in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎間進士，自知縣擢河南道御史。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, he was promoted from magistrate to Censor of the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the Chongzhen reign and rose from magistrate to Henan Circuit censor.

sentences.zh: 為大學士陳演所構，遣戍。

translations.literal: He was framed by Grand Secretary Chen Yan and sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Chen Yan framed him and he was sent into exile.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，薦起原官，以憂歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was recommended and restored to his former post, then returned home on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he was recommended back to his former post, then went home to mourn.

sentences.zh: 三年，复補浙江道御史，仍掌河南道事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was again appointed Censor of the Zhejiang Circuit, still handling affairs of the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he was reappointed Zhejiang Circuit censor while continuing to handle Henan Circuit affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏言：「有司朘削小民，督撫徇不以告。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized, saying: "Local officials squeeze and shave the common people, while governors indulge them and do not report it.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 6 he wrote: "Local officials bleed the common people dry, and governors indulge them without reporting it.

sentences.zh: 言官論劾，乃其職守。

translations.literal: For censorial officials to impeach by discussion is their duty.
translations.idiomatic: It is the duty of censorial officials to speak out and impeach.

sentences.zh: 乞付廷臣公議，勿遽下獄對理。

translations.literal: I beg that the matter be referred to court officials for public deliberation, and not hastily sent to prison for trial.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that such cases be referred to court for open deliberation, not rushed straight to prison.

sentences.zh: 」上從之，諭：「惟挾仇誣陷，仍奪官治罪。

translations.literal: " The emperor assented and instructed: "Only where one bears a grudge and makes false accusations shall office still be stripped and punishment imposed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and ordered: "Only those who lodge accusations out of private vendetta shall still be stripped of office and punished.

sentences.zh: 自非然者，雖有不實，不得迳送刑部。

translations.literal: If it is not so, even where there are inaccuracies, they may not be sent directly to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, even when charges prove partly unfounded, memorialists may not be sent straight to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 」八年，疏言：「文武全才難得。

translations.literal: " In the eighth year he memorialized, saying: "Men fully accomplished in both civil and military affairs are hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: " In Shunzhi 8 he wrote: "Men equally skilled in civil and military affairs are hard to find.

sentences.zh: 近以武職改任督撫，恐政體民瘼未必曉暢，請還本職。

translations.literal: Recently military officers have been transferred to serve as governors; I fear they may not understand government institutions and the people's afflictions—please restore them to their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers have lately been made governors-general and governors, yet they may not understand governance or the people's hardships; I ask that they be returned to their original posts.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「貪吏坐贓，多委諸吏役，遇赦輒復原官。

translations.literal: " He also said: "When corrupt officials are convicted of embezzlement, the blame is often shifted onto clerks and runners; when amnesties come they are usually restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: " He also argued: "When corrupt officials are convicted of bribery, they often blame their clerks and runners, then regain office at the next amnesty.

sentences.zh: 請將援免諸人應左降者，調補閒曹；

translations.literal: I request that those spared by amnesty who ought to be demoted be transferred to idle posts;
translations.idiomatic: Those spared by amnesty who ought to be demoted should be transferred to idle posts;

sentences.zh: 應奪官者，勒令休致。

translations.literal: those who ought to be stripped of office should be compelled to retire.
translations.idiomatic: those who ought to lose office should be forced to retire.

sentences.zh: 」下部議行。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministries were ordered to deliberate and act.

sentences.zh: 是年值計典，煊以河南道掌計冊，劾御史李道昌、王士驥、金元正、匡蘭兆、李允嵒等巡方失職。

translations.literal: That year fell on the triennial evaluation; Xuan, holding the evaluation register for the Henan Circuit, impeached Censors Li Daochang, Wang Shiji, Jin Yuanzheng, Kuang Lanzhao, Li Yunyan, and others for dereliction on provincial tours.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the triennial evaluation. Xuan, holding the Henan Circuit evaluation register, impeached Censors Li Daochang, Wang Shiji, Jin Yuanzheng, Kuang Lanzhao, Li Yunyan, and others for failing their provincial tours.

sentences.zh: 時大學士洪承疇掌都察院，甄別諸御史，議道昌降調，士驥等均奪官，並列煊外轉。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou headed the Censorate and screened the censors; it was proposed that Daochang be demoted and transferred, Shiji and the rest stripped of office, and Xuan likewise listed for outside transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou then headed the Censorate and screened the censors: Daochang was demoted and transferred, Shiji and the others were stripped of office, and Xuan was also marked for outside transfer.

sentences.zh: 煊疏劾吏部尚書陳名夏，以故明修撰，諂事睿親王，驟陟尚書，父為縣民所殺，賜銀歸葬。

translations.literal: Xuan memorialized impeaching Minister of Personnel Chen Mingxia: formerly a compiler of the Ming, he fawned on the Prince Regent and was abruptly promoted to minister; his father was killed by county people and silver was granted for burial and return home.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan memorialized against Minister of Personnel Chen Mingxia—a former Ming Hanlin compiler who had fawned on the Prince Regent and been abruptly promoted to minister. When county men killed his father, the court granted silver for burial and leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 名夏夤緣奪情，卹典空懸。

translations.literal: Mingxia used connections to seize exemption from mourning, and the mourning rites hung empty.
translations.idiomatic: Mingxia used his connections to avoid mourning, leaving the prescribed rites unperformed.

sentences.zh: 因舉紊亂銓序，把持計典，列十罪、二不法，並及名夏與洪承疇、陳之遴於火神廟屏左右密議，承疇送母回籍未先奏，亦非法。

translations.literal: He then cited disorder in appointments, control of the evaluation, listing ten crimes and two unlawful acts, and also noted that Mingxia with Hong Chengchou and Chen Zhilin had held secret discussions at the Fire God Temple with attendants dismissed; Hong Chengchou sent his mother home without first memorializing, which was also unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: He charged disorder in appointments and manipulation of the evaluation, listing ten crimes and two unlawful acts. He also accused Mingxia, Hong Chengchou, and Chen Zhilin of secret talks at the Fire God Temple with attendants sent away, and noted that Hong Chengchou had sent his mother home without first memorializing—all unlawful acts.

sentences.zh: 疏下王大臣勘奏。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to princes and ministers for investigation and report.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to princes and ministers for investigation.

sentences.zh: 時上方出獵，巽親王滿達海等召名夏、承疇與煊質，名夏事俱實，承疇言火神廟集議，即為甄別諸御史，送母回籍未先奏，當引罪。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was out hunting; Prince Xun Mandahai and others summoned Mingxia, Chengchou, and Xuan to confront one another. Mingxia's matters were all true; Chengchou said the Fire God Temple gathering was for screening the censors, and that sending his mother home without first memorializing called for self-accusation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was away hunting. Prince Xun Mandahai and others summoned Mingxia, Chengchou, and Xuan to confront one another. Mingxia's offenses were confirmed. Chengchou said the Fire God Temple meeting was to screen the censors, and that sending his mother home without memorializing first was his own fault.

sentences.zh: 上還京，復命王大臣廷鞫，吏部尚書譚泰袒名夏，奏名夏事在赦前；

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, princes and ministers were again ordered to try the case in court; Minister of Personnel Tan Tai shielded Mingxia, reporting that Mingxia's offenses fell before the amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, princes and ministers were ordered to retry the case in open court. Minister of Personnel Tan Tai shielded Mingxia, arguing his offenses predated the amnesty;

sentences.zh: 煊奏不多實，且先為御史不言，今當外轉，挾私誣衊，罪當死，因坐絞。

translations.literal: Xuan's memorial was largely not substantiated; moreover, as a censor he had earlier said nothing, and now facing outside transfer he bore a private grudge and made false accusations—the crime deserved death, and he was sentenced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's charges were largely unsubstantiated. As a censor he had said nothing before, and now, facing outside transfer, he was accused of lodging false charges out of spite—a capital offense. He was sentenced to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，譚泰得罪，上復發煊疏，命王大臣覆讞，名夏坐奪官。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year Tan Tai fell from favor; the emperor again issued Xuan's memorial and ordered princes and ministers to review the verdict; Mingxia was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Shunzhi 9 Tan Tai fell from power. The emperor reopened Xuan's memorial and ordered princes and ministers to review the case. Mingxia was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 語詳名夏傳。

translations.literal: The account is detailed in the biography of Mingxia.
translations.idiomatic: See the biography of Chen Mingxia for details.

sentences.zh: 遂下詔雪煊冤，贈太常寺卿，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued clearing Xuan's wrongful conviction, posthumously appointing him Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and granting funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then cleared Xuan's name, posthumously appointing him Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and granting state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 以贈官官其子基遠，官至禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: By virtue of the posthumous office his son Jiyuan received appointment and rose to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiyuan received office through the posthumous appointment and rose to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：國初言事侃侃，以開心為最。

translations.literal: =【Commentary】= The commentary says: In the early state those who spoke on affairs were forthright, and none surpassed Kaixin.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In the founding years memorialists spoke with forthright candor, and none surpassed Zhao Kaixin.

sentences.zh: 義、起龍皆用言事致顯擢，克簡巡方著聲績，命岳策屯田雖未用，要自有所見。

translations.literal: Yi and Qilong both rose to prominence through memorializing; Kejian won renown on provincial tours; Mingyue's plan for military colonies, though not adopted, showed insight of its own.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi and Lin Qilong both won promotion through outspoken memorials; Zhu Kejian earned renown on provincial tours; and though Wang Mingyue's plan for military colonies went unused, it showed real insight.

sentences.zh: 森先、裀、開生以謇直蒙譴，獨森先復起。

translations.literal: Senxian, Yin, and Kaisheng were punished for blunt integrity; only Senxian was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Li Senxian, Li Yin, and Ji Kaisheng were punished for blunt integrity; only Senxian was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 煊死非罪，世尤哀之；

translations.literal: Xuan died for a crime he did not commit, and the age especially mourned him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan died for a crime he did not commit, and the age mourned him all the more;

sentences.zh: 然挾外轉之嫌，授讒人以隙，與森先諸人不同矣。

translations.literal: yet bearing the suspicion of outside transfer, he gave slanderers an opening—different from Senxian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: yet facing outside transfer, he gave his enemies an opening—unlike Senxian and the others.
